#483. As Van Hollen wages a challenge, Senate Democrats are torn on whom to elect as their leader

📅 13 Nov 2026

As Van Hollen wages a challenge, Senate Democrats are torn on whom to elect as their leader

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/13/democrats-midterms-senate-leader

Maryland senator’s bid against Chuck Schumer for leadership could decide direction of the Democratic party.

Ever since Donald Trump returned to the White House, Democratic officeholders and voters alike have been divided over whether their leader in the Senate, Chuck Schumer, is up to the task of taking the president on.

That debate intensified on Thursday, when the Maryland senator Chris Van Hollen announced he will challenge Schumer for the post of Democratic Senate leader, which will become one of the most powerful jobs in Washington when the party takes control of Congress’s upper chamber next year.

Diungkapkan bahwa the contest between schumer and van hollen is the party’s first major test of unity after its triumph in last week’s midterm elections, in which voters gave democrats their biggest majorities in both the senate and house of representatives in years. Now the party will be forced to confront the two veteran lawmakers’ differing visions on how to use their newly expanded power to confront Trump, advance the party’s agenda and address divisive issues such as the question of aid to Israel.

Diungkapkan bahwa “trump’s policies have been fired, but we are still in the position where we need to take advantage of this opportunity. So that does mean closing the trust deficit? … And I don’t think you can close the trust deficit by simply returning to the status quo,” Van Hollen said at a press conference on Friday.

Berdasarkan laporan, progressive groups have cheered the 67-year-old van hollen’s candidacy, and he’s picked up a handful of endorsements in the hours since he made his bid official. But his prospects are unclear: the senator said he is an “underdog” in the contest, which is set to be decided at a behind-closed-doors caucus meeting scheduled for 1 December.

Schumer, meanwhile, has expressed confidence he’ll win the Democratic caucus’s nod again, and has the support of senators from across the party’s ideological spectrum.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead,” schumer, 75, wrote on x after van hollen announced his bid. “I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a new york city native, schumer won election to the house in 1980, then the senate in 1998. He became the top Senate Democrat in 2017, when the party was in the minority at the beginning of Trump’s first term. Four years later, Schumer became majority leader under Joe Biden, and managed to win passage of parts of his legislative agenda even though the Democratic caucus was so small it could not lose a single vote on party-line bills.

Sebagaimana diketahui, trump returned to power in 2025, and it was not long after that schumer’s leadership came into question. In March of that year, Congress faced a deadline to approve new government funding or cause a shutdown. Though many Democrats believed they had leverage over Trump to win concessions, perhaps over the gutting of the federal government by the “department of government efficiency”, Schumer opted to advance a GOP-backed spending measure, arguing that it was a bad time to shut down the government.

The compromise triggered an explosion of anger at Schumer both from Democrats in the House of Representatives who had rejected the funding compromise, and activist groups who saw it as a sign that Schumer was no longer fit to be leader.

Diungkapkan bahwa “senator schumer has contributed to and led many important accomplishments that indivisible is grateful for. But with our democracy on the line, he let us, the country and the Democratic party down,” said Ezra Levin, co-executive director of the network of progressive groups.

Berdasarkan laporan, “senator schumer should step aside as leader. Every Democrat in the Senate should call for him to do so, and begin making plans for new leadership immediately. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the relationship between schumer and the party base – including some democratic lawmakers – has yet to recover. Another wave of calls for Schumer to step down arrived later that year, when dissident Senate Democrats decided to end a record-long government shutdown without Republicans meeting any of their demands on healthcare.

Diungkapkan bahwa schumer did not publicly endorse their deal, but it was widely believed to have his backing. By the time campaigning for the 2026 midterms began, several candidates were making their opposition to him prominent in their platforms.

Berdasarkan laporan, in some ways, the tension is a unique consequence of the differences in power between the minority party in the house and senate. In the former, the party out of power has little recourse to block legislation, but in the latter, the filibuster’s 60-vote threshold makes Schumer a major figure in deciding whether his party plays along with the 53 Republicans in the majority, or obstructs them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at the same time that schumer’s standing among democrats was growing rocky, van hollen’s star was ascending. Elected to the Senate from the House in 2016, Van Hollen made national news when he traveled to El Salvador to meet Kilmar Ábrego García, a Salvadorian who had been wrongfully deported from Maryland in the early days of Trump’s mass deportation campaign.

A deep dive into the policies, controversies and oddities surrounding the Trump administration.

Diungkapkan bahwa he has joined in criticizing israel, amid a wider backlash among democratic voters towards the us ally fueled by accusations it committed a genocide in gaza. Van Hollen voted against providing bulldozers and bombs to the country, and after a visit to the Gaza-Egypt border in 2025, co-released a report accusing Israel of planning to ethnically cleanse the territory. In September, the senator led an unsuccessful resolution to force the state department to issue a report on violence in the West Bank.

Berdasarkan laporan, schumer’s criticism of israel has been comparatively muted – he did not vote for the efforts to cute off arm sales, but did support van hollen’s resolution on the state department report. When he was majority leader in 2024, and thereby the highest-ranking Jewish official in the US government, Schumer called on the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, to step aside.

Sebagaimana diketahui, last week’s sweep of the midterm elections seems to vindicate his leadership of senate democrats – after all, the party won just about every state it was contesting, and some where it had invested few resources. Yet Van Hollen said Schumer could have done better, noting that several candidates he had backed in the primaries wound up being rejected by voters.

Diungkapkan bahwa after the election, reports emerged that van hollen was not planning to challenge schumer, fueling speculation that he would instead run for president in 2028. He now says he’s not interested in a presidential run, and announced the bid for party leader just as activists again called for Senate Democrats to replace Schumer.

“Our members are tired of politicians content with incrementalism – they want bold, creative leadership that will help Democrats usher in affordability and accountability without delay or compromise in the next Congress,” said Joel Payne, the executive director of liberal group MoveOn.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we welcome and will support any potential senate leader willing to meet the moment. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a small number of democratic senators have publicly backed van hollen since he announced his leadership bid, including bernie sanders, the independent progressive who caucuses with the party, and incoming senators abdul el-sayed of michigan and peggy flanagan of minnesota. Others, such as Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, incoming senator Adam Hamilton of Kansas and Juliana Stratton of Illinois, said the party should choose a new leader, but have not said who that should be.

#494. 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision

📅 13 Nov 2026

'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw20xmy0m5yyo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Watch: Cruise ship seen sinking after collision with cargo ship in New Orleans.

Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker.

The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel, Atlantic Asphalt.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but us coast guard captain melanie burnham said: "there seems to be some type of a loss of steering. ".

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference that all credit in the rescue effort went to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help".

"We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said.

Calls about the collision came in around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans Chief Melanie Montroll told the news conference.

There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to Port of New Orleans.

Passengers began disembarking from the paddlewheeler vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, as it started listing before tipping on to its side, Mayor Moreno said.

Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help and officials shut down the Mississippi River for the search effort.

The American Heritage was finishing an eight-day cruise to Mississippi River destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi.

President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that the rescue was an "incredible job".

Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said the US Coast Guard also supported local rescue operations.

Governor Jeff Landry also hailed the rescue as a "miracle on the Mississippi" given the "sheer number of people who were on that cruise ship" who were rescued.

Ships have operated safely on the Mississippi River for years, Landry said, pledging to investigate what happened.

Jamie Holford, a witness to the crash, told the BBC's US partner CBS that he saw the cruise ship hit the dock following the collision.

Berdasarkan laporan, "it sounded like a war movie. Just imagine tons of steel crunching. "It looked like something off the Titanic. That's what it sounded like," he said. ".

Holford added that he saw passengers and crew members "hollering" and "crying" as they tried to get off the ship while it was sinking.

The American Heritage can carry up to 150 guests and features a glass-enclosed restaurant, fitness centre and three guest lounges, according to its website.

Built in 2015, the vessel has at least four decks.

#500. Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

📅 14 Nov 2026

Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwm2mn272nqlo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Diungkapkan bahwa jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?.

In 2015, a young male gorilla named Jojo took his first tentative steps onto grass.

Sebagaimana diketahui, until that moment, the 11-year-old ape had spent almost his entire life in a tiny cage at a private zoo in gabon, after being taken from the wild as an infant. His family had been killed by the poachers who took him.

Diungkapkan bahwa more than a decade later, jojo is settled into a sanctuary â but he still lives alone. He hasn't had a family since he was taken, or indeed any gorilla friends.

Diungkapkan bahwa jojo's carers at the lekedi foundation in gabon want to find a companion - possibly another rescued or zoo-bred gorilla â that jojo could live and bond with. But finding him a friend - and bringing them into his life - is not straightforward.

"He's probably the most extreme case of isolation I've ever seen in a great ape," says Prof Gillian Forrester from the University of Sussex, who is studying Jojo as part of research into great ape psychology and how to help rescued animals recover from trauma.

Jojo's keeper Maxe Anaclet Makaba: 'He definitely feels lonely - you can see it in his eyes'.

Jojo was less than a year old â an infant clinging to his mother â when he was captured and sold.

Most gorillas spend the first 14 to 19 years of their life in an embedded family unit but he was kept completely alone and on public display at the private zoo that bought him.

Maxe Anaclet Makaba, who is head keeper at Lekedi and sees Jojo nearly every day, says it is clear he "craves human interaction".

"He will even go to the trouble of gathering leaves for us to hold, so that we [trade them] for a treat â to interact with us," he says.

Jojo also calls out when women he knows well visit his enclosure and then leave, making sounds that silverback males use to summon the females in the wild, explains Ãric Willaume, who runs the sanctuary.

When Jojo first arrived at the sanctuary after spending years in a small iron cage, he didn't look directly at people.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, jojo is one of the more than 6,000 african primates estimated to have been bought or sold in the global trade of apes and other primates between 2000 and 2023. Thousands more are trafficked illegally for use as exotic pets, wild meat, and traditional medicine, the Pan African Sanctuary Alliance says. , external.

Experts believe when baby great apes are taken from their group at a young age like Jojo, they are left traumatised.

Berdasarkan laporan, "if they're old enough to understand what happened to them, to understand their family was killed, they just lose the will to live," explains conservationist tony king, from uk charity the aspinall foundation. I never knew where that expression came from, but I've seen it in gorillas. "You see it in their eyes â the light goes out. ".

King â who specialises in rehabilitating rescued great apes â remembers rescuing two infant sister gorillas who were brought to a sanctuary in the Congo Basin.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "they were clinging to each other," he says. "They stayed together in a little tight ball for about three days before they sort of unravelled. I think that's what kept them alive. ".

Sisters Likendze and Matoko clutch each other after they were brought in a wooden crate to the Project Protection des Gorilles sanctuary in the Congo.

Diungkapkan bahwa african charity the gorilla rehabilitation and conservation education (grace) center uses what it calls "gorilla-led" rehabilitation. When the team rescues a young gorilla from the pet trade, they put it with a group as soon as possible so they can socialise and essentially learn to be a gorilla.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but jojo's case is unusual. He is fully mature and showing signs of harmful, chronic stress, according to Forrester.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in a game-changing approach to studying anxiety and trauma in apes, she has used a thermal camera to film jojo's face. This allows her to monitor blood flow, revealing what appears to be a chronically cold nose.

Berdasarkan laporan, it's a sign of a malfunctioning stress response. When any primate â a human, chimp or gorilla - is stressed, blood flow to the eyes and ears increases. It puts them on high alert for danger, but leaves their nose, temporarily, colder. For Jojo, this "nasal dip" as it is known, does not seem to recover.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "being connected to others is incredibly important to our psychology as great apes," forrester says. "Having another individual to share his life with would be so healing for him.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "i would assume other gorillas would help him process this grief and trauma. ".

Thermal imaging of Jojo's face reveals signs of chronic stress, with a persistently cold nose indicating a potentially disrupted stress response.

Dr Katie Fawcett, from the Grace Center, says it's also "essential" for an animal to form social relationships to be considered for release into the wild - which is the ultimate goal for Jojo's keepers.

Diungkapkan bahwa the bonds between gorillas â what we would call friendship - is key to their society, adds dr robin morrison from the university of zurich, who studies the social lives of mountain gorillas. In one recent study, she discovered that female mountain gorillas would seek out females they knew, even if they hadn't seen them for many years, when joining a group.

And she says a big part of a gorilla's normal social life is "just sitting together quietly sharing space".

But Jojo has never been given the opportunity to sit quietly with another gorilla.

Sebagaimana diketahui, no one knows how jojo will react to a companion. Moving an animal from an accredited zoo would be a decision for an international committee and based on genetics, health and the animals' personalities and compatibility.

Any introduction to another animal would be done very carefully â perhaps giving them an object that smells of the other before they see each other.

Berdasarkan laporan, these slow, cautious ape introductions do happen â when an animal moves from one zoo group to another, for example. Forrester has contacted a number of accredited zoos to explore the possibility of doing this for Jojo. But those discussions have fizzled out with no sign of progress.

The problem, she says, is "there aren't clear processes in place to do these kinds of trans-locations".

Encounters between two or more separate gorilla groups are complex social events.

The international rules and processes for moving captive gorillas across international borders - from one zoo or safari park to another - are designed for breeding programmes.

"They're not designed for reintroductions into the wild, or to find companions for animals that might need them," says Forrester.

And because Jojo, who is probably in his 20s, has reached maturity, King thinks it might be too late for him to bond with other gorillas.

"Jojo's situation is unique, but he is probably best where he is," King says, adding that introducing him to another animal could, somewhat ironically, be a source of more stress for him.

Prof Forrester studies Jojo as part of research to understand how our understanding of human mental health - particularly stress and trauma - can be applied to our great ape relatives.

Diungkapkan bahwa being alone is also natural, even relatively common, for mature male gorillas. "When they reach adolescence, they tend to disperse and spend a good chunk of their life on their own. According to Morrison, about a third of adult males are solitary. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa solo males will try to persuade females to form a group with them, but some don't succeed and may feel lonely as a consequence, morrison believes. "If we think of loneliness in an evolutionary context - this mismatch between the social interactions they want and the social interactions they're getting. I suspect feeling lonely is part of the natural, evolutionary drive to attract females. ".

But while those phases â of family life and adult solitude - play a role in wild gorilla society, Jojo was forced into solitary confinement as an infant.

Morrison believes Jojo is probably both traumatised and lonely.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "[in the wild] gorillas move together, find food together, sleep together," she says. "So much of their lives is just being with this group. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa that is what jojo's keepers, forrester, and others want for jojo. A friend. Maybe a female, or a compatible male.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "it would be good for him to have a companion," says keeper makaba. "Because being alone is like being cut off from the world - it's like being in prison.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "having another gorilla there would be a good thing for him. ".

#501. Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever

📅 14 Nov 2026

Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmlydy0xw45wo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba has signalled his intention to run for president in the next elections.

In Uganda's military, even senior generals are finding that their rank offers little protection from the wrath of the country's powerful army chief.

Over the past 15 months, at least a dozen generals and senior officers have been arrested under Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is also the son of President Yoweri Museveni, in a crackdown that has unsettled the military's top ranks.

The arrests come amid growing political tensions over who will succeed Museveni, who has ruled Uganda for four decades.

Gen Kainerugaba, 52, is widely seen as a potential successor, although his ambitions appear to be facing resistance within the ruling party.

This week, he threatened Vice-President Jessica Alupo with dismissal and possible arrest, while suggesting he should take her position.

The ruling National Resistance Movement (NRM) has, however, rejected reports that its senior leadership had rejected a proposal to back Gen Kainerugaba as the next president, describing the claims as "completely false".

This has all fuelled speculation that the arrests are part of an effort to sideline military officers opposed to the general's presidential ambitions.

Others see the arrests as evidence of an anti-corruption drive in which senior commanders are held to account.

At the centre of the tension are two powerful powerful institutions: the military, where Gen Kainerugaba wields considerable influence, and the NRM, where questions about his political ambitions appear to be dividing senior figures.

A recent meeting of NRM's top leadership ended without agreement on a proposal to position Gen Kainerugaba as Museveni's successor, according to the AFP news agency.

Five party sources who attended the closed-door meeting told AFP that a vote was abandoned after several members spoke against the proposal.

Uganda's news website ChimpReports, however, said that most members who spoke backed the general's potential presidency, although some questioned his readiness for civilian leadership.

In a statement on Thursday, NRM Secretary General Richard Todwong Awany confirmed that the party had met on 10 November to discuss "political, social and economic issues".

He dismissed reports that the meeting had rejected a proposal to position Gen Kainerugaba as Uganda's next president, saying the party would communicate any decisions "through the right channel, at the right time".

President Yoweri Museveni's grandson (standing up, shaking the president's hand) has joined the army, alongside his father (sitting down, wearing camouflage).

Dr Gerald Bareebe, a Ugandan-born political scientist at Canada's York University, sees a connection between the arrests and political manoeuvring over Museveni's succession, often referred to as the "Muhoozi Project".

"Senior officers believed not to support the project have been arrested, detained or charged with corruption and treason," he tells the BBC.

He says the allegations against some officers were widely viewed as politically motivated, reflecting growing divisions within the military over the succession question.

Some of those detained have since been released, apparently after securing the general's forgiveness.

The detention of one of the country's most prominent former commanders, Lt Gen Peter Elwelu, has brought the crackdown into sharper focus.

The former deputy army chief was detained on 2 November over allegations that he had plotted to destabilise the eastern Teso region.

His fall from grace followed a series of social media posts by Kainerugaba, who accused him of treachery and announced that he had been stripped of his three-star rank and demoted.

Diungkapkan bahwa "the traitor peter elwelu is hereby stripped of his ranks. He is demoted to Private," Kainerugaba wrote on X.

He also claimed that more than 20 soldiers linked to Elwelu had been arrested.

The announcement raised legal questions, with Ugandan media reporting that military regulations do not allow a senior officer to be stripped of his rank through a social media post.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the army later confirmed elwelu's detention, saying they had recovered 15 guns, military uniforms and two pickup trucks linked to him. His family has rejected the allegations.

Elwelu is among at least a dozen generals and senior officers detained since April 2025, according to an investigation by Uganda's Daily Monitor newspaper.

They include three former military intelligence chiefs who once oversaw some of Uganda's most sensitive security operations.

This army chief threatened to castrate opposition leader and claimed descent from Jesus.

The 'shadow army' helping Uganda's long-serving president keep an iron grip on power.

The Ugandan general who lobs grenades on Twitter.

Maj Gen James Birungi, a former head of defence intelligence and security, was arrested in August 2025, on allegations including treason, terrorism and corruption.

He was charged before a military court but later released after Gen Kainerugaba announced that he had "forgiven" him.

Sebagaimana diketahui, another former intelligence chief, maj gen abel kandiho, was detained in september this year over allegations of providing false intelligence and treachery. He remains in detention, according to the Daily Monitor.

His predecessor, Brig-Gen Charles Bakahumura, was also arrested in September over similar allegations, but was later released after the army chief announced that he had forgiven him.

Other officers have faced accusations ranging from stealing military fuel to taking money to spy on military communications.

The military has defended the arrests as part of efforts to tackle corruption and criminality within the armed forces.

Maj Gen James Birungi was arrested in August 2025, on allegations including treason, terrorism and corruption.

Ugandan security analyst Freddie David Egesa says the arrests reflect investigations involving different security agencies, rather than an army-led purge.

He argues that detaining senior officers helps protect witnesses and demonstrates the seriousness of the anti-corruption drive.

Diungkapkan bahwa "gen muhoozi has the overall duty to permit the investigation team to arrest these high-profile people, in consultation with the commander-in-chief," egesa says, adding: "the arrests are not summarily done. ".

But Bareebe sees a wider political motive, arguing that officers suspected of opposing to Gen Kainerugaba's presidential ambitions are being targeted.

"The result is a broad purge that has affected both serving and retired officers perceived to be anti-Muhoozi," he says.

He points to divisions between the elite Special Forces Command (SFC), which he says is largely loyal to the president's son, and army commanders who remain unconvinced about his succession.

The allegations against the officers are at different stages, with some facing charges, others in detention without publicly announced charges, and several having been released.

Bareebe also questions whether military trials can deliver independent proceedings.

"Many Ugandans regard the charges as politically motivated and therefore expect little justice," he adds.

He alleges that some officers have had charges dropped after closed-door negotiations with the president and his son, during which they were pressured to declare support for Gen Kainerugaba.

Government spokesperson Allan Kasujja dismissed the claims of a succession fallout as "hogwash".

Berdasarkan laporan, unlike his predecessors, who communicated through official military channels, gen kainerugaba frequently uses x to announce arrests, criticise public officials and comment on domestic and international affairs. Some have sparked diplomatic controversy.

On the night of 9 November, he turned his attention to Vice-President Jessica Alupo, demanding to take her job.

"Whoever is in that office should prepare to hand it over soon," he wrote, in posts that he later deleted.

He also questioned Alupo's loyalty and threatened her dismissal, adding that the government would operate "on military terms", if he became his father's deputy.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the following day, his x account, which had nearly 1. 4 million followers, became inaccessible.

It was unclear whether he deactivated it himself, which he has done before, or the platform had suspended it.

Alupo remains in office and has yet to respond publicly.

Vice-President Jessica Alupo is yet to respond to Gen Kainerugaba's posts questioning her loyalty.

Egesa says Gen Kainerugaba's controversial posts reflect his preferred style of communicating, but adds that security analysts are assessing their implications for Uganda's political and military stability.

Bareebe, however, sees them as part of a broader effort by the army chief to extend his influence into civilian politics.

He says the public confrontation with senior political figures illustrates how the succession debate was spilling beyond the army and into the ruling party.

Gen Kainerugaba was appointed army chief in March 2024, after previously commanding the SFC, which is responsible for protecting the president and strategic installations.

Under Uganda's military structure, he reports directly to Museveni, giving him considerable influence over the army.

Bareebe argues that the SFC's loyalty to the president and his son could prove crucial in any future transfer of power.

"The regular army remains important but has been sidelined by the SFC, which now functions as a personal army for Museveni and his son," he adds.

At the heart of the tension is the question of who will succeed Museveni, 82, who has ruled Uganda since 1986, when his rebel National Resistance Army seized power after a five-year guerrilla war.

He was sworn in for a seventh elected presidential term earlier this year, extending his rule into a fifth decade.

Gen Kainerugaba has been regarded as a possible successor and has indicated that he intends to seek the presidency in 2031, when his father's current term is due to end.

He also leads the Patriotic League of Uganda, a political movement that has mobilised support around his leadership.

But recent developments suggest that a transfer of power from father to son may be more complicated than his supporters anticipated.

At the recent meeting of the NRM leadership, one official reportedly urged Museveni to retire his son from the military and give him a civilian role to gain administrative experience, AFP reported.

Local media reported that some party officials consider Gen Salim Saleh, Museveni's younger brother, better suited for civilian leadership.

There is, however, no indication that he is interested in becoming president.

Others reportedly defended Gen Kainerugaba, pointing to his military leadership, anti-corruption campaign and grassroots political mobilisation.

Bareebe says opposition to the proposed succession has grown within the NRM, with both veteran figures and younger members concerned about what they see as an attempt to secure power through coercion.

He suggests Museveni's reluctance to move his son out of the military could reflect the importance of retaining control of the army during any transition.

"The underlying calculation appears to be that, so long as Muhoozi controls the SFC, he can use it to capture power even in an event of a contested transition," he says.

The military has been central to Museveni's hold on power, making the loyalties of senior commanders particularly important as succession questions intensify.

The family's military influence has also drawn attention to the possibility of a political dynasty spanning generations, with Gen Kainerugaba's son, Ruhamya, recently graduating from Britain's Sandhurst military academy.

The succession debate is unfolding against a backdrop of sustained pressure on the opposition.

Veteran opposition politician Kizza Besigye remains in detention on treason charges, which he denies.

Bobi Wine, who came second to Museveni in this year's presidential election, has gone into exile in the US, after being threatened by Gen Kainerugaba.

The government has consistently defended its security operations as lawful and necessary to maintain stability.

But the arrests, his son's threats and competing accounts of divisions within the ruling party have intensified questions about how Uganda's next political transition might unfold, and what role his family may play.

#502. Stuart Bonds made ‘racist’ and ‘divisive’ comments. But One Nation is showing no sign of dumping the NSW candidate

📅 14 Nov 2026

Stuart Bonds made ‘racist’ and ‘divisive’ comments. But One Nation is showing no sign of dumping the NSW candidate

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/14/one-nation-nsw-candidate-stuart-bonds-ntwnfb

The former coalminer’s claim Australians are being ‘demographically replaced’ sparked wide criticism, but his party has shown no signs of dumping him.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

In a Facebook video from a Sydney anti-immigration rally on Sunday, as a man dressed like a medieval knight watches on, One Nation’s lead upper house candidate, Stuart Bonds, launches into a speech against “mass” migration.

“Make no mistake, we are being demographically replaced inside our own nation,” he says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “if we don’t support australian mothers having australian children, we [are] going to pay for other cultures’ children to be brought up in our lands. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in an apparent allusion to the “great replacement theory”, a far-right conspiracy theory that white westerners are being actively “replaced” by minority ethnic immigrants, he continued: “that’s the socialist plan, is to destroy and bring down and tear down the fabric of your civilisation. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the comments sparked a wave of criticism, but the party has shown no signs of taking bonds off the ticket for the 2027 new south wales state election. One Nation did, however, dump one candidate this week: the Victorian branch disendorsed a lower-house candidate over an old social media post describing Hitler as the “GOAT”, an acronym for greatest of all time.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the rally was not a one-off. On a podcast released on Monday with the rally’s organiser, the Australian Lobby Group, Bonds appeared to double down on the remarks. He did not challenge host Scott Challen’s assertion that Labor governments were building “ethnic voting blocks with Middle Eastern and subcontinent people … to stack the numbers to entrench power for themselves”, instead responding: “Mate, and that’s why we’re going to get rid of all of the multicultural grants, right?”.

Diungkapkan bahwa on wednesday, in an interview with abc upper hunter, bonds responded to questions about his comments by citing australian bureau of statistics data that shows the proportion of australians born overseas has trended upward since the end of the second world war, from 10% in 1945 to 32% in 2025. He did not mention that the proportion of Australians born overseas was at its highest – 32. 4% – in 1891, the first year of available data.

Diungkapkan bahwa bonds said with the australian birthrate beneath the 2. 1 required to replace the population, “I would just like to know what people assume is going to happen. ”.

“Where are these people going to come from?” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nsw labor pounced on the rally comments immediately, with the state’s premier, chris minns, calling them “frankly outrageous and racist”. The government passed motions in both houses censuring Bonds, not yet a member.

Berdasarkan laporan, the coalition followed four days later. On Wednesday afternoon, the opposition leader, Kellie Sloane, said Bonds’ language was “clearly divisive”.

But she did not rule out a confidence and supply arrangement with One Nation after the March state election.

“We will not form a coalition with One Nation, [but] we’ll work with anyone post-election if we’re in a minority government,” she told reporters.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the australian financial review has reported many of her mps privately expect the party to go into a coalition with one nation. And with the Coalition consistently polling behind One Nation, that makes Bonds not a fringe candidate, but a potentially influential figure.

The ABC’s former election analyst, Antony Green, said the remarks played straight into Labor’s hands.

“This will certainly be something the Labor party uses in all those multi-ethnic seats in Sydney,” he said – seats like those on the rural fringes of Sydney, which One Nation said it plans to target.

Indeed the deputy premier, Prue Car, who has Indian heritage and whose electorate of Londonderry is one of the seats in question, gave an impassioned critique of Bonds’ comments in question time on Tuesday.

Diungkapkan bahwa “who’s he [bonds] talking about when he talks about this?” she said. “I tell you who he’s talking about – he’s talking about families like mine, and families that I represent. ”.

Kos Samaras, a former Labor strategist who is now a director of polling group Redbridge, said that while the comments likely won’t play well in Sydney seats – including alienating moderate Liberal voters worried about the party going into Coalition with One Nation – “you might be able to get away with it in certain parts of NSW”.

And Bonds, a former coalminer, has made his base in the Hunter.

Samaras said One Nation could “clean the deck” in the regions, including Labor-held seats in the Hunter, and “pretty much anything else the Coalition hasn’t got bolted down to the ground”.

The NSW One Nation leader, Mike Newman, who in September said he “made a mistake” when he told a Sydney rally he wanted to stop abortions, did not respond directly when asked if he agreed with Bonds’ comments or if he would rein in his first-placed upper house candidate.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “what i will say is that what stuart bonds is a patriotic aussie. He’s a coalminer. He has very, very strong views,” he said on Tuesday.

Diungkapkan bahwa newman, who previously rejected claims that one nation was racist, said on tuesday: “what we want to do is … protect australian values, and that is the fundamental thing that stuart bonds is pushing for. It’s about assimilation. ”.

The NSW treasurer, Daniel Mookhey, whose parents immigrated to Australia from India in the 1970s, told the ABC that Bonds’ comments were not grounded in reality.

“I think he’s saying that there is a deliberate conspiracy to use migrants to replace the way he puts it, native-born Australians for political reasons,” Mookhey said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the quota for election to the upper house is 4. 5%, making Bonds all but guaranteed to be elected, with One Nation polling in the high 20s and low 30s in recent months.

Green expects the party to pick up four or five seats in the upper house; so far it has only named three candidates: Newman, Bonds and Jeff Bacon, a firearms manufacturer who is second on the upper house ticket.

But unlike Victoria, NSW has optional preferential voting, which means when that state goes to the polls in March, lower house preference flows aren’t guaranteed.

But Bonds has downplayed whether he may have jeopardised a future preference deal with the Coalition.

“If the Coalition have a problem with facts, the same as the Labor party, then maybe it will,” he told the ABC.

Berdasarkan laporan, “but i’m not here to impress the coalition. ”.

#504. A ‘Generational Clash’ Is Fueling Europe’s Protests

📅 14 Nov 2026

A ‘Generational Clash’ Is Fueling Europe’s Protests

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/14/world/europe/student-protests-pensions-generations.html

Berdasarkan laporan, as retirees live longer, governments need to spend more on pensions. That makes it harder to fund other services, spurring protests like those planned this weekend in France.

Sébastien Ducros, a French data analyst who supports the widespread student protests in his country, has identified an obvious culprit for the lack of government funds for dilapidated schools.

Diungkapkan bahwa “a huge portion of the money is going toward retirees, while many other things are being neglected,” said mr. Ducros, 36. “I honestly think — even if it feels strange to say — that people like my parents are in a position where they should and could” surrender some of their pension payments, he added, saying that they were about to retire.

Berdasarkan laporan, but laurent grinwald, 72, who retired recently after decades as a postal worker, isn’t eager for his pension to be reduced, particularly to pay for other state-funded services. Especially, he said, as rents and the cost of living have shot up.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we’ve been working all this time,” mr. Grinwald said, “and now, suddenly, the stance is, ‘Well, no, we’re going to start taking a bit more?’”.

Diungkapkan bahwa this disagreement embodies a broader question for europe, one that is at the heart of mass antigovernment demonstrations planned for saturday in france, as well as recent protests driven by frustrated young people in countries including belgium, germany, greece, italy and portugal. As Europeans live longer, should the needs of the young be eclipsed by their parents’ and grandparents’ pensions, routinely the largest items in Europe’s national budgets?.

“It’s a generational clash,” said Jorge Galindo, the director of EsadeEcPol, an independent think tank in Spain, which has some of the most generous pensions in Europe.

#505. After a summer win, India's Gen Z protesters face a winter of uncertainty

📅 13 Nov 2026

After a summer win, India's Gen Z protesters face a winter of uncertainty

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq99e0z4vg1eo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

India's Gen Z protesters are facing the limits of dissent.

Cheers erupted at Delhi's Jantar Mantar protest site in July as news broke that Gen-Z protests had forced federal education minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one protester turned to me, beaming: "this is the youth's victory. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, just over three months later, the mood has shifted dramatically. Student protesters are now struggling even to assemble. Demonstrations by the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) last month over voting rights were met with sweeping restrictions and thousands of peaceful protesters were detained.

The summer had seen a new wave of dissent in India, driven by deep frustration among the youth and fuelled by irreverent online satire.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the movement spread across the country, and prime minister narendra modi, a leader with a strongman image, unaccustomed to open criticism or mockery, struggled to contain it. But the government's increasingly forceful security response suggests it has learned from its rare concession to protesters, invoking public order to curb dissent.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the ruling bharatiya janata party (bjp) national spokesperson syed zafar islam rejected accusations of heavy-handedness and told the bbc: "the right to protest and freedom of expression is mandated by the constitution, but it has to be done within the law. It cannot override the rights of others, at the cost of public security".

This is by no means the first time the Modi government has faced large-scale protests.

But the breadth of them pose a challenge for the BJP, according to Yamini Aiyar, former president of the Centre for Policy Research and visiting professor at Brown University.

The CJP led massive protests in July which ended with the resignation of a federal minister.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "they are not defined by caste, gender or economic class," aiyar said. "Even some of the core BJP base, the upwardly mobile, lower-income classes, were attracted by the movement. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the scale of the youth protests is also magnified by its online presence. Protesters have broken a longstanding political taboo, openly mocking the prime minister online.

"It's more than just laughs," said Sakhi, a student protester who identifies as they/them and affiliated with one of Delhi University's left-wing student organisations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the fear of repercussions in other generations isn't felt as much in ours," they said. "Comedy is a new language to challenge authority. ".

Previous protest movements posed serious challenges to Modi but were easier to dismiss as representing narrow sections of society or to label "anti-national", according to Aiyar.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in 2020, farmers protesting against controversial agricultural reforms were blocked from entering delhi, leading to months of demonstrations and, at times, clashes on the capital's borders. After a year of protests, the government abandoned the reforms.

Protests against a contentious citizenship law in 2019 and 2020 are a stark reminder of the powers of the judiciary should anyone be deemed a national security threat.

Sebagaimana diketahui, student activist umar khalid was arrested under anti-terror laws after violent clashes in delhi that killed 53 people, mostly muslims. He was accused of being a "key conspirator". He has now spent more than six years in jail without his trial having begun.

His partner Banojyotsna Lahiri told the BBC they have no regrets, but that the situation instilled "a kind of fear that has prevailed".

The CJP in its early days became a unifier for Indian youth frustrated with the state of education, jobs and economy.

Berdasarkan laporan, "we are just looking at a very dark mesh of empty space, because we don't know when the endpoint is," lahiri said. Khalid's latest appeal was lodged this month.

Aiyar believes opponents are using a familiar "playbook" today to "de-legitimise" protests, but that it isn't resonating as convincingly.

Nevertheless, the youth protests have struggled to recapture this summer's momentum.

Sebagaimana diketahui, cjp leaders, including spokesperson saurav das, have faced repeated detentions and legal action. Das and fellow leader Ashutosh Ranka spent a week in Delhi's Tihar jail after being accused of trespassing at Jantar Mantar.

The site of their summer victory has since been struck off the list of authorised protest venues, a decision being challenged in court.

Protesters from other groups, including the left-wing All India Students' Association (Aisa), have also faced police action over allegations of defying orders.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we were expecting some kind of crackdown," said das. He added that "the government has learnt a lot" since the summer.

Legal experts warn the proceedings themselves can have a chilling effect.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "a lot of cases can lead to acquittals, but it can take years. The process is the punishment, and that can deter protesters," said Ali Khan, an assistant professor at Lloyd Law College.

The restrictions on demonstrations have become excessive, according to constitutional lawyer Vrinda Grover, who is advising the CJP.

Tens of thousands of people gathered at Delhi's iconic Ramlila Maidan for the opposition protest on 1 November.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "those who are organising the protests have repeatedly emphasised that this is non-violent," she argued. "Rights have been whittled down in the name of law and order. ".

The BJP has rejected suggestions it is suppressing peaceful dissent.

Islam told the BBC that demonstrations "cannot override the rights of other citizens just because a handful of people want to protest and be responsible for violence".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, even dissenting online carries risk. Sakhi's viral social media posts have attracted targeted abuse and transphobic attacks. The BBC has seen posts threatening them with violence and rape.

Sometimes, it can deter Sakhi from protesting or even make them change the way they dress.

Diungkapkan bahwa "making people laugh can turn into being called anti-national," sakhi said. "They want me to feel damaged," they added.

They claim some of their content was removed after getting millions of views.

Berdasarkan laporan, under india's information technology laws, the government can order platforms to block content on national security grounds. Notices on X and Instagram have shown accounts being withheld in India.

CJP leaders have likened the crackdown to the 1975 Emergency, when then prime minister Indira Gandhi suspended civil liberties and jailed political opponents.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, opposition parties have, in part, filled the void. Tens of thousands gathered in Delhi on 1 November for a rally organised by INDIA bloc, an alliance of opposition parties led by Congress, and permitted by the authorities.

CJP leaders, meanwhile, insist the movement is bigger than their organisation.

When Das walked out Delhi's Tihar prison on 21 October, photographs showed him smiling.

Berdasarkan laporan, "i would just say wait and watch," das told us. We are a very young generation. "Time is on our side. ".

#506. Microsoft ‘deeply sorry’ for global disruption that could have billion-dollar impact on Australia

📅 14 Nov 2026

Microsoft ‘deeply sorry’ for global disruption that could have billion-dollar impact on Australia

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/14/microsoft-deeply-sorry-for-global-disruption-that-could-have-billion-dollar-impact-on-australia

Experts say outage exposes ‘Australia’s reliance on foreign technology’ as software giant says services being restored.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

The Microsoft outage could be a disaster for the Australian economy that forces some small businesses to close, with costs expected to run into the billions of dollars, experts have warned.

The US software company has said it is “deeply sorry” for a widespread outage that caused disruption to millions of users, organisations and businesses across the globe – and that it has “addressed the underlying issue”.

The company said the outage was a “technical issue” not related to cyber-attacks or AI agents, and that it continued to gradually restore services.

Experts have said the outage exposes “Australia’s reliance on foreign technology” and that people unable to be paid, send an invoice, or access government services “are entitled to be worried”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the outage of microsoft’s services, which began on friday morning, lasted roughly 18 hours before services started to recover. Microsoft said it was bringing back services gradually to ensure a stable restoration.

Ashwin Pal, a partner at the risk advisory firm RSM Australia, said his clients had activated business continuity and disaster recovery plans, but many businesses didn’t have a fallback.

“A protracted event like this can easily be the straw that breaks the camel’s back for smaller entities,” Pal said.

Pal said Microsoft had obviously struggled to recover, which raised bigger questions.

“I’m a technologist and I’m actually flabbergasted as to how something like this could have happened … they pushed out a change which should have been tested,” Pal said.

The Australian Computer Society has renewed calls for the federal government to urgently review which critical IT systems rely on a single provider, and where backup options could keep the economy running.

The society’s chief executive, Prins Ralston, said the outage had “exposed Australia’s reliance on foreign technology”, particularly on small businesses.

“Australians who couldn’t get paid, couldn’t send an invoice, or couldn’t reach a government service this morning are entitled to be worried,” Ralston said.

Australian hospitals and health clinics were affected by the outage, although the Australian Medical Association (AMA) on Friday said had been no impacts for patient care.

“We’ve had some facilities return to using paper for scripts because authentication to get into lots of prescribing software requires multifactor verification, which requires you to be able to access your Microsoft-supported email,” said the AMA’s president, Dr Michael Bonning.

Diungkapkan bahwa courts in south australia and victoria reported that the outage had affeced its email system. Many schools across the country were also affected.

Service NSW, the one-stop shop agency for residents, drivers, and business owners to access government services, encouraged customers to delay their visits to its service centres.

Federal government departments have also been maffectedy the outage, including national security agencies.

The head the domestic spy agency Asio, Mike Burgess, on Friday said the organisation’s systems “operate on multiple levels”, adding that they had been affected “on one level, yes, but not completely”.

The outage has affected businesses and organisations across the world that use Microsoft products.

In the UK, healthcare systems were disrupted and several British police forces urged people not to try to report crimes online and to phone them in instead.

Sebagaimana diketahui, us government offices across the country have been affected by the outage, including congressional offices that heavily rely on outlook email. The US House’s chief administrative officer that handles IT for the chamber sent out a “campus-wide alert” to staffers on Thursday about the outage, Politico reported.

In Japan, the shipping company Sagawa Express said it was unable to accept online reservations for some of its services at airports and train stations while Taisho, a leading pharmaceutical company, said it was having to handle orders by phone.

Diungkapkan bahwa when stock market trading opened on wall street, shares in microsoft dipped slightly, down 1. 1% at $516. 86.

Microsoft has suggested the outage may have been caused by problems with the settings applied to servers responsible for keeping Microsoft 365 up and running.

Diungkapkan bahwa microsoft’s executive vice-president of copilot, charles lamanna, said: “we regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the issue. ”.

Two Celebrity Cases Put a Spotlight on British Courts’ Gag Orders

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/14/world/europe/russell-brand-david-walliams-gag-order.html

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, russell brand and the tv personality david walliams both persuaded courts to suppress misconduct allegations against them. Some say the libel laws need to change.

Two recent cases have brought new attention to the ways that British laws can allow the wealthy and powerful to silence their critics.

Berdasarkan laporan, the first was the rape and sexual assault trial of the comedian russell brand. Brand has denied her allegations. Before his conviction last week, Mr. Brand had obtained an injunction prohibiting another accuser from telling almost anyone — including the police, her family and most doctors — about her claims that he assaulted her. (Mr. ) That injunction, first revealed by Dan Neidle, a tax lawyer and free-expression activist, apparently remains in force.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the second instance, two british news organizations were temporarily blocked from reporting allegations of sexual misconduct against david walliams, a television personality and author of children’s books, before a judge declined to make the injunction permanent. The Guardian newspaper and ITV News, a British broadcaster, published investigations last week into the allegations, which Mr. Walliams denies.

Berdasarkan laporan, though both men now face public scrutiny, the revelations of how they used court injunctions — essentially gag orders — to protect their reputations have provoked no shortage of public and political outrage. Judges in other cases have issued “super injunctions,” which prohibit publishing any information even about the injunction itself.

“What will the government do to prevent these abuses of process, and stop the abusive injunctions and super injunctions which stop scrutiny, accountability and the work of the free press?” Nick Timothy, the shadow justice minister, asked in Parliament on Tuesday.

The British government is now “looking at what we can do,” Alex Davies-Jones, the government minister responsible for victims of crime and violence against women and girls, said in response.

#508. University hounded out of Hungary by Orbán reaches out to new government

University hounded out of Hungary by Orbán reaches out to new government

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/14/university-hungary-orban-soros-ceu

Prospect of partial return to Budapest by Central European University suggests confidence in Hungary’s future.

A university that Viktor Orbán tried to chase out of Hungary is open to expanding its presence in Budapest, in a mark of confidence in the country’s democratic future.

Carsten Q Schneider, the interim president and rector of Central European University (CEU), said it was interested in increasing its programmes in Budapest, as long as this did not damage the student experience.

So far the CEU has not held formal talks with Hungary’s new government, which has promised to restore academic freedom, “but our hand is reaching out, their hand is reaching out – it is just that they have many things to do”, the academic told the Guardian.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the ceu relocated its main activities to vienna from budapest in 2019, after pressure from the previous government led by orbán. But the outlook changed when Péter Magyar won a landslide victory in April pledging to root out corruption and reform the state.

The CEU, founded by Hungarian-American financier and philanthropist George Soros in 1991 to entrench democratic change in the region, was forced to cease awarding degrees in Budapest in response to a law widely seen as targeting the institution.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the eu’s highest court struck down hungary’s “lex ceu” in 2020, finding that it violated the eu charter of fundamental rights, but the verdict came too late for the university. The CEU retains 312 staff in Budapest, mostly administrative, but the majority, 476, and all its teaching, are in Vienna.

Diungkapkan bahwa schneider said upgrading the status of the ceu, which is privately funded, in budapest would be “a symbol for academic freedom [and] of resilience” but depended on goodwill and funding independent of the hungarian government. He said a decision on its future in Hungary would be taken by the CEU’s 13-member board, whose members include Soros and his son, Alexander Soros.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we don’t want special treatment,” schneider said. ‘“We are a great asset, so let’s work out something. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, but the ceu, which he said was “thriving tremendously” in vienna, does not plan a wholesale return to budapest. Any change would have to ensure the quality of the student experience, for instance, assuring that students would be able to combine courses, say in economics and history, without having to travel the 200km-plus distance between the two cities.

Focused on social sciences, law and humanities, the CEU has more than 1,400 students from 103 countries, mostly doing master’s and PhD programmes.

Berdasarkan laporan, according to schneider, for the first time in the ceu’s 25-year history, students from the us now make up the largest cohort of master’s students (10%). The CEU has seen an increase in US applicants since Donald Trump returned to the White House and launched a sweeping campaign against elite universities, including slashing federal funding and seeking to exert control over internal policies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the ceu rector has had informal talks with us academics on how to maintain academic freedom under pressure from rightwing populists. These people have a plan, so it’s not by accident that they attack universities. He described his message as: “Don’t be naive for a second. They want to have cultural hegemony. ” He added, however, that Trump and allied movements, such as Germany’s Alternative für Deutschland, have identified “real problems”, such as in the US how universities have entrenched “a reproduction of elites”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when coming under political pressure, he said universities needed “to look for allies”, among other academic institutions, students, alumni and parents. Institutions also had to stand up for disciplines under attack, such as gender studies, Schneider added.

The most pressing stories and debates for Europeans – from identity to economics to the environment.

He recalled the outpouring of support for CEU – when tens of thousands of people protested in Budapest in defence of the university – as “one of the most humbling experiences I have had”.

Schneider, a German political scientist who specialises in the study of democracies and regime transition, said Magyar had successfully used Orbán’s political machine against him.

Berdasarkan laporan, “nobody has a better idea than [magyar] how to defeat the most potent and the most skilled illiberal populist [orbán]. So he knows something. ” He added: “The people and skills that you need to bring a non-democratic regime down are not the same and sometimes the opposite of what it takes to establish a democracy. So the question now is whether he [Magyar] has the skills to basically reinvent liberal democracy for the 21st century. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, schneider said hungary could be the world’s first “post-illiberal democracy” – a model for democratic restoration, just as orbán inspired rightwing populists around the world. But he also raised doubts about this thesis, saying there were questions about how Magyar and his Tisza party might develop in the context of Hungary’s “very difficult economic situation”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the test would be, he suggested, when magyar faces losing support and, eventually, defeat at the ballot box. “So what happens when he loses support and then cracks in his movement appear? Will he be the visionary leader who manages … to establish a three, four, five-party system, where people compete? That is to be seen. ”.

#510. ‘It’s frustrating’: chaos at US airports as stoppage grinds travel plans to a halt

‘It’s frustrating’: chaos at US airports as stoppage grinds travel plans to a halt

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/13/us-airports-flight-stoppage

Travelers and crew feeling ‘pissed’ or ‘lucky’ depending on level of upset amid nationwide ground stop.

Airport chaos continues after FAA lifts ground stop – live updates.

The US Federal Aviation Administration’s decision to ground all flights on Friday threw airports and travel plans into chaos across the country, as passengers on planes and in airport terminals were suddenly thrust into limbo.

At New York’s John F Kennedy airport, passengers found their travel plans abruptly cancelled – some even after they’d boarded.

Steve Honberger, heading home to Portland, Oregon, with his wife and daughter, said he’d been on a plane about to take off when the shutdown was announced.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “they didn’t seem to know what’s happening, and they wanted to hold off as long as possible,” honberger said. The plane sat at the gate for an hour and 40 minutes.

They realized they were just going to be sitting at the gate, so they eventually asked to deplane and rebook.

Sebagaimana diketahui, many still thought it worth showing up despite the uncertainty of when flights would resume. Rashid Kahn, heading for Miami, said he’d “heard about the ground stop on the news, but the airline said we might take off 10 or 11pm”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i am hopeful,” he added. “But maybe it’s something to do with the date. I’m not super serious, but it’s Friday the 13th. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, tom rolenaitis, returning a shiba inu show dog named tsuki to finland, said it was frustrating. We have no idea what’s happening. “It’s cutting into a three-day trip and I have to get him back to his owner. ”.

A flight attendant headed for Barcelona, who declined to give his name, said he had been told his American Airlines flight would be slightly delayed and all incoming international flights were being allowed to land.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, another crew member from the flight said cheerfully: “things happen. Hopefully it will all be resolved. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as the day wore on, passengers on international flights began to be boarding, prompting applause to erupt at the gates. “But only international is going. “It’s moving, so that’s good,” said an airline representative. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the faa issued the nationwide ground stop on friday afternoon, citing a communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, according to an faa notice. Four hours later, FAA sent out an advisory lifting the stop.

Berdasarkan laporan, “you can’t moan about this kind of thing. She still hoped her flight would go. it’s such a first-world problem,” said Laura, a woman who lives in New York and was heading for San Francisco when her JetBlue flight was grounded. “That what I have to figure out,” she said, sitting on the floor of the terminal.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with the lifting of the ground stop, more chaos followed. “My flight was cancelled, then I go to a kiosk, put my information in and it says I’m leaving at 3am. Then I talk to the desk and they know nothing,” said Larson Welsh, heading to Las Vegas from Paris.

Berdasarkan laporan, the outage has nonetheless caused upheaval for thousands of passengers. There have been 10,343 flight delays within, into or out of the US so far, according to the website FlightAware, and 1,479 cancellations. More than 1,000 aircraft were bound for US when the ground stop was announced, according to Flightradar24.

Only two national ground stops have previously been issued: on 11 September 2001, after the terrorist attack on the World Trade Center; and in January 2023, after a communications failure.

Berdasarkan laporan, the ground stop also snarled the sports world, leaving nba, nhl and college teams stranded as they tried to reach their destinations before a big weekend of games. It also was unclear whether referees, who typically fly to their assignments the day before games, would make it on time.

Back at JFK, travelers expressed frustration and resignation.

Diungkapkan bahwa “my flight to california was cancelled with no information and no rebooking. “It’s frustrating. My flight was cancelled last night as well due to bad weather. Now I’m missing a family event,” said a man who gave his name only as Andy. And I’m pissed. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa honberger, meanwhile, tried to stay optimistic, saying: “there are people sitting on tarmac, so we count ourselves lucky and we were able to book ourselves a hotel for the night. ”.

Tom Johnson and agencies contributed reporting.

#511. SpaceX Starship megarocket blasts off before expected return for reuse

SpaceX Starship megarocket blasts off before expected return for reuse

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026/nov/13/spacex-starship-megarocket-blasts-off-earth-orbit

Flight 15 expected to orbit Earth about 14 times over 22 hours, before company catches it at Starbase, Texas.

SpaceX’s Starship megarocket blasted off from Texas on Friday afternoon as the aerospace company sought to make history with a double catch of its reusable rocket, but ultimately fell short.

Starship, the world’s largest rocket, standing at 407ft, is expected to orbit Earth about 14 times over the course of 22 hours, before the company catches the rocket at its launchpad at Starbase in south Texas.

The rocket, which is on its 15th flight, is composed of two elements: the lower booster, with 33 Raptor engines that fired off during takeoff, and the Starship at the top.

As smoke plumes wafted from the launch site, SpaceX employees erupted into cheers.

Diungkapkan bahwa spacex had planned for both components to return to its tower, but the booster, named super heavy, was aborted, and splashed down in the gulf of mexico. The cause of that diversion remains unknown.

“That certainly isn’t the news that we had hoped to hear for today,” said Kate Tice, SpaceX’s director of quality management, but she noted the booster’s return was in line with “rigorous safety checks”.

Berdasarkan laporan, early in the webcast, spacex simulated the return. The entire rocket was expected to be grabbed in the launch tower’s “chopstick” mechanical arms.

Friday’s test did not rise to the double-catch mantle, which Elon Musk had described early in November as a “critical breakthrough needed to make life multiplanetary”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, still, the flight is still poised to mark another milestone for the company. If all goes to plan, it would be the first time SpaceX has caught the rocket’s 171ft upper stage.

Previous tests focused on the retrieval of the booster.

The Starship, meanwhile, has continued to sail through space at over 26,000 km/h at an altitude of 270km.

The launch went on as scheduled despite a nationwide ground stop that disrupted hundreds of flights.

Flights to the west coast from Hawaii were temporarily paused, then resumed on Friday due to space debris from the launch, according to the island’s transportation agency.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as in the past, starship carried satellites for starlink, spacex’s internet service wing, three of which were fitted with cameras to analyze the rocket’s heat shield. The data plays a role in determining if the spacecraft is ready to return.

SpaceX chief executive Musk has sought to advance Starship’s “rapid reusability” as a vehicle, which he hopes will take humans to the moon and, controversially, to Mars.

Nasa has contracted SpaceX, along with Jeff Bezos’s Blue Origin, to provide the lunar landers that will return astronauts to the moon in 2028.

Musk has cast his reusable rocket as a buffer against the enormous costs associated with future space travel.

SpaceX has launched a flurry of test flights in recent years, some of which have resulted in explosions that signaled major design flaws.

In September, the most recent flight test, SpaceX notched a victory, sending the spacecraft into Earth’s orbit for the first time, although its engine failed during the ascent.

#518. Choking fires, deadly heat and devastating floods: 2026 in extreme weather

📅 14 Nov 2026

Choking fires, deadly heat and devastating floods: 2026 in extreme weather

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/14/fires-heat-floods-extreme-weather-2026

People around the world have contended with unprecedented weather events and their fatal effects caused by the climate catastrophe.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after the world’s hottest summer since records began in 1850, the death toll from extreme weather in 2026 is already in the high tens of thousands. That is a conservative estimate and is certain to rise much higher.

As Cop31 continues and scientists warn that climate breakdown may be accelerating, the Guardian looks back at a year of droughts, fires and floods as a reminder that, unless the world takes urgent action to cut emissions, this disastrous year will be one of the best of the rest of our lives.

Berdasarkan laporan, extreme heat fuels wildfires in australia as temperatures jump nearly 20c (68f) above average, victoria and other southern states register new heat records, including 50c in port augusta and the tiny opal mining town of andamooka. Scientists say the supercharged climate has made the heatwave five times more likely. Melbourne hospitals report a 25% increase in heat-related illnesses, while authorities in many areas struggle with wildfires. Heatwaves already cause more deaths in Australia than all other natural hazards combined.

Diungkapkan bahwa mudslides kill 72 in brazil after record rain the city of juiz de fora in minas gerais records its wettest ever month, triggering landslides that sweep away hundreds of homes in poor communities on unstable hillsides. Floods also disrupt Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo. More than 10,000 people are displaced.

Berdasarkan laporan, devastating floods across much of the world in ethiopia, at least 131 people are killed in floods and mudslides that bury entire villages. Eighty die in Kenya and 18 in Tanzania. Many areas report record rainfall. Flood waters in southern Russia submerge homes and leave more than 300,000 without electricity. At least 30 die in Afghanistan as heavy rains trigger landslides. The Arabian peninsula is battered by fierce winds and heavy downpours that flood the streets of the desert kingdom. Hailstones the size of tennis balls fall in Oman and lightning storms leave cities in the UAE inundated with water. Hong Kong is soaked in twice the usual monthly precipitation. Huge tracts of farmland are left underwater in Argentina and Chile.

Berdasarkan laporan, world’s energy imbalance accelerates rapidly the world meteorological organization reveals an alarming buildup of energy in earth’s system. António Guterres, the UN secretary general, says: “The global climate is in a state of emergency. Planet Earth is being pushed beyond its limits. Every key climate indicator is flashing red. This makes weather more extreme and threatens health and food supplies. ” Guterres urges the world to cut fossil fuel emissions as rapidly as possible to minimise future risks. More than 90% is stored in the oceans, where warming has more than doubled over the past two decades compared with the average over the previous 45 years. However, CO2 in the atmosphere continues to rise.

Berdasarkan laporan, super typhoon tears through micronesia, guam and saipan at peak intensity on 12 april, sinlaku registers a wind speed of 295km/h (183mph) – roughly the same as a shinkansen bullet train and the joint highest recorded by a storm in the western pacific basin so early in the year. It is also the deadliest in decades, killing 12, leaving 43,000 without power, forcing mass evacuation and causing $1. 5bn (£1. 1bn) in damages. This will remain one of the most powerful storms of 2026, superseded only by Super Typhoon Champi that will strike Taiwan and Japan in October.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hundreds of millions endure deadly heat in south asia at least 47 heat-related deaths are reported in southern asia as temperatures soar above 45c in several indian and bangladeshi cities, and hit a peak of 52c in pakistan’s southern province of sindh. Scientists warn that the climate crisis is exposing hundreds of millions of people in south Asia to longer, deadlier pre-monsoon heat.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ocean heat enters uncharted territory sea surface temperature graphs begin to jag upwards and away from all previous highs on 21 june, starting a trend that will worsen over the rest of the year. This alarms scientists because oceans absorb more than 90% of the excess energy in Earth’s system. If the seas start to release that heat then the land and air will get warmer more quickly.
