Hungary: Millions in hidden cash found in Orban graft probe

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.dw.com/en/hungary-millions-in-hidden-cash-found-in-orban-graft-probe/a-79946923?maca=en-rss-en-all-1573-rdf

Diungkapkan bahwa investigators discovered bundles of banknotes buried in forests and concealed in buildings. The money was seized during an investigation into a former minister accused of accepting millions in bribes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hungarian authorities have recovered nearly $20 million (€17. 7 million) in hidden cash during a corruption investigation into a former minister under ex-Prime Minister Viktor Orban.

The country's newly established National Asset Recovery and Protection Office said Friday that investigators discovered the money during searches linked to former National Development Minister Miklos Sesztak.

The discovery is part of a sweeping anti-corruption campaign launched by Prime Minister Peter Magyar, who defeated Orban in April's parliamentary election.

The money was discovered during two days of searches in the capital, Budapest, and three Hungarian counties.

Investigators found large quantities of cash buried in forests, concealed in agricultural buildings, warehouses and residential properties, as well as stored in an expensive safe at a secluded location.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the recovered money included 5. 3 million), €2. 3 million, $15. 66 million (€2. 07 billion Hungarian forints (€13. 9 million) and $1. 26 million (€1. 08 million).

According to Finance Minister Andras Karman, 12 employees of the Hungarian State Treasury spent eight hours counting the banknotes using five counting machines.

The agency also released a video showing investigators kneeling beside large piles of bundled cash and digging into the ground in what appeared to be a forest at night.

Authorities said the seized money had been deposited into an account belonging to the Hungarian state treasury.

Sesztak served as Orban's national development minister between 2014 and 2018.

He is suspected of accepting more than $37 million (€33 million) in bribes and kickbacks connected to the purchase of overpriced used buses by state-owned transport companies and state construction projects.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the former minister was taken into police custody in late september. He has denied wrongdoing.

His lawyer, Gabor Papp, so far did not respond to a request for comment on the latest discovery.

Magyar described the recovered cash as a turning point in his government's efforts to tackle alleged corruption under Orban.

The discovery "officially marks the end of the Fidesz-KDNP mafia," he wrote on Facebook, referring to Orban's former governing coalition.

Diungkapkan bahwa "as of today, viktor orbán is a proven mafia boss. A fallen mafia boss. And Fidesz is a criminal organization," Magyar added.

Magyar's center-right, pro-European Tisza party won a landslide victory in April, ending Orban's 16-year rule.

The new prime minister has pledged to repair Hungary's relations with the European Union, which had been strained by years of disputes under Orban.

His government established the anti-corruption agency with investigative and prosecutorial powers to pursue suspected corruption and misuse of public funds.

Diungkapkan bahwa magyar has dubbed the campaign "operation purgatory. ".

Several other senior figures from Orban's time in office have been detained as part of separate investigations.

Among them is former central bank governor and economy minister Gyorgy Matolcsy, once considered one of Orban's closest allies.

Berdasarkan laporan, matolcsy is being investigated over the alleged misuse of a central bank foundation that received 288 billion forints ($818 million, €787 million) in public assets. He and other former officials under investigation have denied wrongdoing.

Police also detained Orban's younger brother earlier this week as part of an investigation into suspected human trafficking and influence peddling.

Sebagaimana diketahui, orban has condemned the investigations as political "tyranny" aimed at removing him from hungary's political landscape. He has described his brother's detention as an act of political revenge.

Berdasarkan laporan, according to a survey by pollster median published by news website hvg this week, 70% of respondents considered the anti-corruption campaign "very important. ".

A separate Median survey showed support for Orban's Fidesz party had fallen to 16% of voters by November, roughly half its level before the April election.

#562. Sudan: Misery worsens amid plummeting aid for displaced people

Sudan: Misery worsens amid plummeting aid for displaced people

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.dw.com/en/sudan-misery-worsens-amid-plummeting-aid-for-displaced-people/a-79938864?maca=en-rss-en-all-1573-rdf

Diungkapkan bahwa sudan's humanitarian crisis is exacerbated by cuts in international aid. Almost 34 million people are in need as war and drone strikes are making it difficult to deliver aid to the population.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the international organization for migration (iom) and the united nations high commissioner for refugees (unhcr) are sounding the alarm: serious funding gaps have depleted the supplies of emergency shelter and basic household goods intended for sudan. Without urgent provision of flexible funding, even more families will have to cope without adequate protection from extreme weather conditions, insecurity, violence and exploitation in the coming months.

Berdasarkan laporan, according to a recently published joint statement, $2. 62bn) is needed for the United Nation's Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan. 9 billion (€2. 4 million people in Sudan. This funding is intended to provide life-saving aid to 20. So far, however, only 47% of the required funds have been raised.

Diungkapkan bahwa a total of 33. Some 15. 4 million alone require emergency shelter and basic household items. 7 million people in the war- and famine-stricken country are dependent on humanitarian aid. However, due to a lack of funding, aid organizations have been able to assist only 10%.

Sebagaimana diketahui, more than three and a half years after the war began between the sudanese armed forces (saf) and paramilitary rapid support forces (rsf), sudan is still the site of the world's largest humanitarian and displacement crisis. 6 million people fled within the country to escape the escalating violence and more than 4. Another 5. 6 million fled to neighboring countries. However, their towns and infrastructure have been destroyed. About 8. 2 million have returned to their regions of origin despite the ongoing war. Fighting, drone strikes and logistical problems further complicate the delivery of humanitarian aid.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, between 40,000 and 250,000 people have been killed. Accurate or updated figures are not available as fighting continues, satellite-based internet communication is curbed, and many aid organizations and observers have left the country.

Berdasarkan laporan, "it's hard to imagine how people are supposed to survive," marina peter, chairwoman of the sudan and south sudan forum in germany, told dw. In large parts of the country, people have been cut off from humanitarian aid since the war began. Some have survived by eating roots. According to the Sudan expert, the fact that people are still returning to war zones from neighboring countries is also linked to shortages: Food rations have been drastically cut in refugee camps.

Diungkapkan bahwa ivo körner, sudan specialist at caritas international, criticizes the international community for the sharp decline in aid. "Globally, we're seeing a dramatic drop in funding for humanitarian aid," Körner told DW. It's not just the United States that has slashed its contributions; Germany and the European Union are also providing significantly less funding than they did four or five years ago, he said.

Diungkapkan bahwa in sudan, caritas international supports refugees and the communities hosting them with cash assistance, drinking water supplies, basic medical care and seeds. However, Sudan's Caritas' projects in 2026 have been financed exclusively through donations. While Körner hopes for additional funding from the German Foreign Office for Sudan projects, he predicts that funding opportunities will be significantly more limited than in previous years.

Diungkapkan bahwa according to sudan expert marina peters, the consequences of the crisis are becoming increasingly difficult to assess. Peter also notes that child mortality in Sudan is above average. "In many parts of the country, people have already been completely cut off from humanitarian aid since the start of the war," she told DW. However, it is nearly impossible to determine the actual extent of the crisis more precisely because the warring parties continue to obstruct humanitarian access.

Berdasarkan laporan, on october 23, the united kingdom and 31 other international partners, including germany, issued a joint statement on the looming famine in sudan. The countries are calling on the warring parties to allow unimpeded access for humanitarian aid and to refrain from attacks on civilian infrastructure. 5 million people — about 41% of the population — are suffering from acute food insecurity. According to the statement, 19. At the same time, they are demanding an increase in international aid funding.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while marina peter welcomes the appeal in principle, she sees a contradiction. "The question is: Who is this appeal actually directed at?" Most of the signatories have themselves systematically cut funding for humanitarian aid and development cooperation. The appeal to the international donor community is thus ultimately directed at the states themselves.

Meanwhile, the Sudanese government based in the country's capital Khartoum — led by General Abdel Fattah Al-Burhan's SAF — rejects all warnings of a famine.

Berdasarkan laporan, in a statement dated october 26, it claims that the food situation in the country is reportedly reassuring and that government reserves and ongoing agricultural production are sufficient to meet demand. According to Khartoum, the warnings from Western countries amount to a politicization of the humanitarian situation.

Berdasarkan laporan, peter criticized this statement as "truly cynical and almost perfidious. The government's claim that humanitarian organizations have unrestricted access also does not reflect reality, she said. In many places, aid continues to be obstructed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in addition to hunger and displacement, the threat to civilians posed by the use of drones is also growing. In the first three weeks of October alone, at least 306 people were killed in attacks. The Peace for Sudan Platform issued an appeal on November 5 calling for an end to attacks on civilians, markets, hospitals, and water and electricity supplies. According to the UN Human Rights Office, drones claimed the lives of at least 1,120 civilians in the first half of 2026.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "drone strikes are a major problem," caritas' körner confirmed. This makes local partner organizations all the more important, he said. They cause widespread anxiety among the population and often strike civilians. Added to this is the danger to humanitarian workers. They enjoy the trust of the local population, are deeply rooted in the regions and in some cases are able to reach areas that international aid workers can hardly access.

#567. Philippines’ Carmelle wins first Eurovision contest in Asia

📅 14 Nov 2026

Philippines’ Carmelle wins first Eurovision contest in Asia

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2026/nov/14/philippines-carmelle-wins-first-eurovision-contest-in-asia

Filipino entry, pop and rap song Sobra-Sobra, takes 19-year-old to victory at grand final in Bangkok.

Carmelle Collado has won the first Eurovision song contest Asia, taking the Philippines’ entry, Sobra-Sobra, to victory in Bangkok on Saturday night, at the first regional edition of the contest to be staged outside Europe.

Eleven countries competed at the One Bangkok Forum in central Bangkok, and the show ran for two and a half hours including advertising.

Berdasarkan laporan, the winner, who performs under the single name carmelle, finished on 211 points, 41 clear of the hosts thailand, with vietnam third. She received the most votes from both the national juries and the public ballot.

Carmelle, 19, grew up beside the railway tracks in the Bicol region of south-eastern Luzon and has been competing in televised talent contests since she was 12.

Sobra-Sobra mixes pop and rap, is supported by traditional Philippine instruments, the kubing and kulintang, and is sung in Tagalog and English.

After her victory, Carmelle said her song celebrated female empowerment and was intended as “a tribute to all Filipino women”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i made history, since this was the first time,” she told the associated press. “It’s such a big responsibility for me, because this one is a global stage, so thank you everybody who voted for me. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “it’s about how unapologetic, independent and strong filipinas are,” she told the guardian before the final. “It describes me – not just me, but of course all the Filipinas. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the show opened with a routine celebrating the host country, in which muay thai fighters shared the stage with drag performers on street food carts. The 11 acts were then driven on in tuk-tuks, each carrying their national flag.

Berdasarkan laporan, vietnam’s tóc tiên, a star at home for more than 20 years, performed first, among dancers costumed as lotus leaves. Mang x Daou represented Thailand, a duo assembled for the contest in the host country who performed a duet staged like a musical number.

Nepal’s Pratik Himal Rai gave one of the most conventionally Eurovision performances of the night with Ananta Maya, a rock ballad staged with fire imagery and a large heart-shaped structure behind him.

Berdasarkan laporan, he ended it by appealing for support for his country, which he said was “going [through a] very hard situation”. More than 1,500 people were killed and more than 5,000 were reported missing after a rock and ice avalanche near the Chinese border triggered catastrophic flash floods in August.

Berdasarkan laporan, bangladesh’s beatmosphere, originally a nine-member a cappella and beatbox group, sang without a single instrument. Three of their members were left out of the final due to a rule capping each act at six performers on stage.

Berdasarkan laporan, nyendra from bhutan sang dressed in the gho, his country’s national dress for men, against a backdrop of himalayan peaks. Mongolia’s Beck performed in a reinterpreted deel, also a national costume.

Sebagaimana diketahui, half the result was decided before the show began. The 11 national juries voted at a dress rehearsal on Friday night and put the Philippines at the top with 93 points, ahead of Vietnam and Malaysia.

The other half came from viewers around the world, who could vote online but not for their own country, and who were given eight free votes each and the option to buy 10 more.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, laos’s entrant, thinla, was unable to hear her own music during her performance, and her dress rehearsal was aired once all live performances were over. She finished fifth, with the night’s third-highest public score.

Carmelle receives no prize money but does get a trophy presented by Dara, the Bulgarian singer who won this year’s European contest, and will perform at Eurovision 2027 in Burgas.

Organisers have said the right to stage future editions will not automatically go to the winner, on the grounds that smaller countries lack the infrastructure.

Some of the clearest echoes of Eurovision’s camp traditions came through those who announced the votes.

South Korea’s jury points were read by Jo Kwon, a veteran pop star who has played Adam in the Korean production of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert and the title role in Everybody’s Talking About Jamie.

The Philippines’ were read by Vice Ganda, a gay comedian who is one of the biggest stars on Philippine television.

Meanwhile, the guest performer was the Thai singer Jeff Satur, who reached a wider Asian audience through KinnPorsche, a 2022 series in the genre of male same-sex romance dramas that has a large following across Asia.

Organisers intend the Bangkok show to be the first of many regional editions, with the executive producer, Assaf Blecher, saying that 16 or 17 territories had expressed interest in competing next year, among them China, Hong Kong and Taiwan.

MPs across factional lines share concerns about policy that legal expert says ‘paints the imprisonment of children as therapeutic’.

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast.

Until December last year, Meena Singh was the Victorian commissioner for Aboriginal children and young people, a role that saw her advocating for some of the state’s most vulnerable children.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, she had held the role since 2022. In all that time, she says, nobody from the Victorian government had approached her with a proposal like the one the Victorian premier, Ben Carroll, announced last week: a $204m “tough love” plan to send children who commit low and mid-level offences to secure facilities, including the former Malmsbury youth justice centre, for schooling, drug and alcohol treatment and life skills.

“If you are on the trajectory of committing crime like carrying a knife or looking to steal cars, you can expect to be detained and be put in this new mandatory detention in Malmsbury,” Carroll told reporters last Sunday.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we have seen how, where you break the cycle, it can turn young lives around. ”.

Singh says she was “quite horrified” by the announcement.

“It is very misleading to try and paint the imprisonment of children as therapeutic,” Singh, now a professor at Monash law school, tells Guardian Australia.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “children who are getting in trouble with the law, there are reasons behind it … imprisoning these children is effectively imprisoning them for traumas they have experienced rather than the behaviours they are displaying. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa she is far from alone in her criticism. The Victorian Aboriginal Legal Service called the announcement “mandatory sentencing dressed up as political leadership” and the Justice Reform Initiative said it was a “dramatically disproportionate response”. The same organisations were among the legal and human rights groups that lashed other Labor changes introduced this term in an attempt to bring down the state’s crime rate – including “adult time for violent crime” and tougher bail laws.

Even the state’s union movement has criticised this proposal, with the Trades Hall secretary, Luke Hilakari, taking to his personal social media account to publicly rebuke the government.

“Honestly thought the policy of locking up children for a year for shopping lifting [shoplifting] or vandalism was from the Liberal party,” he wrote, adding that one of the most common items stolen was groceries.

“How about we fix disadvantage rather than deepening it.

Diungkapkan bahwa “and if you want to win an election, could we leave issues in the liberal party frame to the liberals. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, hilakari finished his post by sharing a demosau poll, released on monday, showing labor on a primary vote of 18% – the lowest figure in its history. That same day, Carroll was in South Melbourne spruiking a $70m plan to hire police reservists to reopen police stations Labor has closed over the term and $300m to build and renovate stations.

Berdasarkan laporan, half a dozen mps from across the party’s factional lines, not authorised to speak publicly, also shared their concerns with guardian australia. Some said Labor was handing the Liberals a free kick by choosing to campaign on crime after presiding over rising crime rates and the closure of police stations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, others say they gritted their teeth and supported the earlier measures, hoping it would be enough to stem the bleeding on the issue. This hasn’t eventuated – a separate RedBridge poll, released on Wednesday, had the party at a 23% primary vote. And it said Labor was 18 points behind the Coalition on crime.

Another Labor strategist, who requested anonymity to speak freely, described the announcement as “a metaphor for the complete lack of clarity regarding our identity and message for Victorian voters”.

The strategist was particularly disturbed to see Davydd Griffths, Labor’s candidate in Melbourne – a seat currently held by the Greens leader, Ellen Sandell – standing behind the premier for the press conference.

“What targeted Melbourne voter would support that policy? The focus on crime this week has scrapped any chance of winning Melbourne off the Greens,” they said.

Diungkapkan bahwa for mps on the right of the party, it’s “too little too late”. They say crime disproportionately affects working-class communities, particularly in the outer-suburban seats Labor needs to retain – and other MPs would’ve known this earlier if they were actually in touch with their constituents.

“This is a reflection that, since the campaign started three weeks ago, they’ve been copping it out door knocking, at street stalls, shopping centres on crime,” one MP said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, those on the left say the proposal is further proof labor has abandoned its values. He’s also sought to distance himself from a government he has been part of for more than a decade. Carroll has pitched himself as a “centrist”, an “economically conservative, socially progressive premier”. The slogan printed on the rear of his big red campaign bus is anything but subtle: “New Premier, New Direction”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the strategy appears to be based on the idea that voters want a decisive break with the past. But there are concerns that, in trying to disown the government’s record, he is also disowning the Labor movement’s achievements over the past 12 years. It risks giving voters little reason to remember why they voted for them in the first place.

One MP said a growing group of colleagues were “furious” that the new leadership had “overseen the trashing of the government’s legacy and instead delivered an election campaign focused almost exclusively on the Big Build royal commission and law and order – two issues losing votes for Labor”.

“Having lost all but our most rusted-on Labor voters to other parties, it looks like they are now happy to see how far we can push before they leave us as well,” the MP said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there’s evidence this is happening. Monday’s DemosAU poll had the Greens at a record high 17%. This was prior to Labor’s move to run an open ticket in Prahran, which has angered progressives.

The Greens responded on Friday by confirming they will be running their version of an open ticket – urging people to put the Greens first and One Nation last rather than direct preferences.

There’s no doubt this will hurt Labor in a number of seats, capping off another difficult week on the campaign trail.

Diungkapkan bahwa benita kolovos is guardian australia’s victorian state correspondent. Henry Belot contributed to this reporting.

McLachlan said any potential compensation arrangements must be considered on an individual basis for each artist, adding it would be difficult to ensure an industry-wide scheme would be fair.

“As a Liberal, I believe property rights are foundational to a healthy democracy and a strong economy,” he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the state should never seek to compulsorily acquire or trade away an individual’s property rights except in very limited circumstances and not without just compensation. ”.

Labor and the Coalition are both in favour of attracting more AI investment and datacentres to Australia, but the opposition has warned the government against “selling out” Australian rights holders in a rush to secure investment.

The growth of datacentres in Australia is expected to increase emissions and power costs for households, prompting backlash from environmental groups and some communities.

McLachlan, who has spoken strongly on conservation and environmental issues, said: “Datacentres must not be built at the expense of our biodiversity.

“We must explore ways to build sovereign AI capability in a sustainable way.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i choose real forests over virtual ones. ”.

#572. How a US extradition bid over Hamas allegations put a wealthy activist before a Spanish court

How a US extradition bid over Hamas allegations put a wealthy activist before a Spanish court

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/14/activist-extradition-gaza-hamas-spanish-court

James ‘Fergie’ Chambers, a Cox Enterprises heir, faced a two-hour hearing about alleged support for Hamas.

A two-hour hearing in Spain’s high court Friday on the US extradition request of wealthy leftwing activist and philanthropist James “Fergie” Chambers turned out to be a study in contrasts.

Chambers’s defense took most of the session to query the US citizen and detail irregularities in the Trump administration’s extradition request – several of which the Guardian has reported on – as well as the figures of Spanish law that would lead the three-judge panel to deny the request; while the prosecutor sped through his case, head down, asking Chambers no questions at all.

Berdasarkan laporan, notably, neither the judges or the prosecutor asked chambers to address the insinuation in the extradition request that the wealthy activist had supported hamas. Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money laundering charge and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but the defense’s queries did allow him to speak for the first time since his 10 july arrest in ibiza about events at the center of the case: 2023 protests against israeli weapons manufacturer elbit in massachusets and new hampshire and 2024 transfers of $7. 2m to Tunisia, where he lived at the time. The latter was buttressed with testimony from a financial expert.

Berdasarkan laporan, on the whole, chambers painted a picture different from the depiction contained in the extradition request, that of a violent backer of hamas on the run from the us. At one point, he noted that his family’s next door neighbor in Tunis was the US ambassador.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the court will decide next week on extraditing chambers. If the decision is affirmative, Spain’s council of ministers can reverse the court’s decision. This means Chambers’s extradition may be among the last decisions made under Pedro Sánchez, the socialist prime minister, before national elections on 29 November.

Berdasarkan laporan, friday’s hearing began with chambers’s defense asking about his wealth. A self-described communist and anti-imperialist, Chambers sold stock back to his family’s business, Atlanta-based Cox Enterprises, worth about $250m in mid-2023.

Berdasarkan laporan, then he started a foundation, he told the court. He and the foundation’s three-member board decide on funding and ensure that no projects seeking support are under US sanctions, Chambers said. The foundation has funded an estimated 100 progressive and humanitarian projects in 20 countries, according to his partner, activist and actor Stella Schnabel – including, Chambers said Friday, organizations in Gaza working on issues such as “medical treatment for children, transportation out of dangerous areas and clean water and food”.

Two of the request’s three charges – riot and conspiracy to riot – are related to the late-2023 protests against Elbit.

Chambers detailed his participation in the protests: locking himself to a door, marching in the street and – in New Hampshire – standing in the road, speaking to the media and paying bail for four protesters who were eventually found guilty of misdemeanor charges and served 30 days in jail.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as for the $7. 2m, the defense and a financial expert serving as a witness laid out how ten bank transfers from the US to Tunisia mostly went to sponsor the football club Club Africain – described by Chambers as “one of the largest football clubs in Africa” – and a sporting business Chambers launched while living in Tunisia.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “is there any indication that the money went to support terrorist activities?” asked defense attorney aitor martínez. “None,” said financial expert Albert Deulofeu Schilt.

Then, in about 15 minutes of rapid-fire monotone, prosecutor Juan Hernández Villalba laid out a wholly different picture of Chambers as backing “an organized structure … aimed at repeatedly committing illegal acts … together with funds destined for terrorist organizations”.

He accused the defense of laying out the facts of the case “in a fragmented way … when what’s most relevant is an evaluation of the whole picture”.

“The extradition petition isn’t based on ideology or political statements, but on actions [Chambers] organized, financed and carried out, causing material damage,” Hernández Villalba asserted.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the actions against elbit “were presented as a simple protest”, he said. “Nevertheless, the actions described by the US were planned for days … with objectively violent content. ”.

Given all this, the prosecutor said, “there are more than enough indications to consider … that [Chambers’s] funding was aimed at terrorism”.

Berdasarkan laporan, among the 100-plus people in varying time zones following friday’s hearing on the court’s youtube channel was irish film-maker and journalist sinéad o’shea, whose documentary on chambers called all about the money makes its new york premiere this weekend. I saw myself the football club in which he invested in Tunisia and his donations to Palestinian and other charities are a matter of public record. It covers the time period cited by the FBI affidavit underpinning the US request. It is impossible not to see this as a politically motivated case. O’Shea said that extradition case “builds a false narrative which begins with the protest in New Hampshire – a piece of vandalism at worst and for which people ended up serving 30 days. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa chambers’s views have been extensively profiled in us media. A week after the 7 October 2023 Hamas attacks on Israel, he posted on X about Israel’s response: “Stop calling it ‘collective punishment’/There’s nothing to be ‘punished’ for/No faction of the Palestinian resistance, Hamas or other, has done *anything* wrong/It’s simply genocide/Like it has been. ”.

Dressed in dark jeans, a grey-blue shirt, a black jacket, with a close-cropped haircut and mustache, Chambers got the last word during the hearing.

“To this day I cannot understand why I have been in prison since July for what amounts to speaking emotionally and committing minor offenses of public disturbance,” he said.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i’ve never had any contact with any terrorist organization. And my wife will give birth, God willing, in March – and I don’t know if I will be by her side. I missed my grandmother’s funeral last week. I’ve certainly never financed any terrorist organization … and for this my family has been torn apart. My five-year-old son asks where I am every day. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “[all] because i have spoken my mind, and i had a lot more money than others who have spoken their mind, in my country. And that’s all it amounts to. ”.

Watch: US ground stop caused by issue during copper wire update, transport secretary says.

A nationwide US ground stop that caused thousands of flight cancellations was caused by an issue following a copper wire upgrade, Transport Secretary Sean Duffy said.

Duffy told a news conference that the government was trying to find out whether the problem was caused by "incompetence" on the part of the company doing the upgrades, or faulty equipment.

The US government does not believe it was as a result of a cyber-attack, although an investigation is still under way, Duffy said.

Friday's suspension was the longest such incident since the 11 September 2001 attacks on the US and the disruption is expected to last for days.

Maintenance was being carried out to switch from copper wire to fibre by a contractor called L3Harris, a technology provider company, Duffy said.

The US has "an incredibly old telecommunications system", he added.

"It was such an old wire that it was being discontinued," he said.

The transport secretary explained that a router that was being worked on had started flooding other air traffic control systems and created communication issues with planes which led the government to shut down the airspace for safety reasons.

Berdasarkan laporan, bryan bedford, who heads the federal aviation administration (faa), told the same news conference: "we see zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything ai related. ".

On Saturday L3Harris said it had completed over 70% of the work to modernise communications infrastructure before the shutdown.

"We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the 13 November ground stop of our nation's air travel," it said in a statement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "l3harris takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travellers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously. ".

'We'll get home one day' - US travellers impacted by nationwide ground stop.

No flights were allowed to take off from the continental US for more than four hours from 15:54 EST (19:54 GMT) on Friday.

More than 3,500 flights were cancelled and more than 2,000 delayed in the US on Saturday, according to tracking website Flight Aware, as knock-on disruption continues.

Italian regulators have fined social media giant Meta â¬805m (Â£670m; $887m) for accessing Android users' photos without their specific consent.

Italy's Data Protection Authority said Meta did not properly inform about 20 million smartphone users that it had access to their photos and videos via a feature of the Facebook app.

It has given Meta 60 days to disable the feature by default and seek users' consent separately.

The fine is among the largest an Italian authority has ever imposed on a tech giant.

The charge is related to a feature which suggests photos and videos from a user's phone gallery as ideas for posts.

Sebagaimana diketahui, facebook requested access to users' photo galleries through a single app-wide authorisation. According to the Italian regulator, a preceding notice did not make clear that this would also allow Facebook to generate suggestions based on photos in their gallery.

More cold health alerts have been issued for parts of the UK on Sunday night and next week.

The alerts were issued by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) for the north-west, West Midlands and Yorkshire and the Humber, and will be in place from 9pm on Sunday until 9am on Thursday.

Berdasarkan laporan, these alerts mean the weather is “likely to have minor impacts on health and social care services”, including an increased use of healthcare services and a greater risk to life for vulnerable people, the agency said. The warning came after forecasters predicted the UK was in for a milder weekend, before another cold snap arrives on Monday.

Paul Coleman, a consultant in public health at the UKHSA, said: “This is the latest cold health alert of the season and we can expect more as we move further into winter.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “cold weather can have a serious impact on the health of some people, including those aged 65 and over and those with pre-existing health conditions, so it is vital to check in on friends, family and neighbours who are most vulnerable. ”.

On Sunday, temperatures are expected to not fall below freezing in the morning, with sunshine forecast in the east and across the far north and west as the day progresses.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on monday, colder weather is expected to return. Sunny skies will appear in patches across the UK, while cold showers are forecast to rain down in the north of the UK. Light snow is also expected in hilly areas in the north.

#584. Philippines wins first Eurovision Song Contest Asia

📅 14 Nov 2026

Philippines wins first Eurovision Song Contest Asia

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqrlgnx9dx6eo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Philippines' Carmelle has won the first Eurovision Song Contest Asia with her women's empowerment anthem Sobra-Sobra.

The Philippines have won the very first Eurovision Song Contest Asia, hosted in Bangkok and with 11 countries vying for the title.

Nineteen-year-old singer Carmelle was always a front runner with her women's empowerment anthem Sobra-Sobra, complete with its catchy rap section.

She earned 211 points in total - 93 from the jury and 118 from the public vote - ahead of Thailand's MANG x DAOU in second place with 170 points.

There was a joyous atmosphere at the One Bangkok Arena as the crowd cheered the contestants and celebrated the popular winner.

Carmelle was the youngest contestant in the comeptions at 19 years old.

Carmelle, the youngest contestant in the competition, was an obvious favourite with the juries and the public despite strong showings from several nations.

Other notable acts included MANG x DAOU, whose emotive duet Aroma elicited huge cheers from the home crowd.

Bangladeshi beatboxers Beatmosphere eschewed the traditional backing track, instead using their voices to replicate the sounds of drums and basslines.

And Laos's Thinla performed her crowd-pleasing song Bae in a traditional Lao hilltribe outfit.

However, the Laotian song had a unintentional second outing after the music video was played over an apparent technical issue during the broadcast - meaning it was the last song the audience heard before the vote.

Thinla wore a traditional Lao hilltribe outfit during her performance.

The voting system worked much the same as the European Eurovison, with the public vote accounting for 50% of the result and the other 50% coming from the 11 national juries - with additional points awarded from a rest of the world vote.

Also performing during the broadcast was 2026 Eurovision Song Contest winner Dara from Bulgaria, who performed her winning song Bangaranga and new song Bad Idea.

Thai superstar Jeff Satur also made an appearance, hitting the high notes in his performance of Black Tie.

Vietnam's Toc Tien came third with 164 points.

Eurovision in Asia was an idea that has been talked about for decades, but one that never seemed to materialise - despite many false starts - until now.

There is a huge enthusiasm here for Eurovision Asia, but a large number of the audience were established fans of the original contest from other countries and regions of the world.

Speaking after the show, fan Zelie Pereira - who travelled from Scotland to Thailand to attend - said she was "very happy" with Carmelle's win.

Eurvosion superfans Michael, Scarlett and Zelie travelled from the UK to Thailand to watch Eurovision Asia's first outing.

Korea, Vietnam and Laos also received praise from Pereira and her friends Michael Peters and Scarlett Massie, both from England.

"It was amazing, a very high standard," said Massie.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the dance was amazing. The singing was amazing. The sets were amazing. The costumes were amazing. Incredible", Peters added.

They confidently declared that "Asia Vision" should be the name for next year's show.

For some, it seems the excitement for another edition is already building.

However the crowd at the One Bangkok Arena thinned out not long after the Philippines singer Carmelle lifted the trophy.

The arena was crowded, but not full, and it's still not clear how much commitment there is among regional broadcasters to keep the contest going and expand it to more than 11 countries.

#586. A rapid interest rate rise seems inevitable – and households are expected to pick up the tab

📅 14 Nov 2026

A rapid interest rate rise seems inevitable – and households are expected to pick up the tab

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/14/interest-rate-rise-phillip-inman-inflation-economy

Raising borrowing costs too far risks laying waste to whatever growth there is in the economy.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a head of steam is building up behind the bank of england raising interest rates again. With the latest forecasts by the central bank showing inflation rising to 5% next spring, another increase in the cost of borrowing seems inevitable, and may come as soon as next month.

A growing number of analysts predict the Bank’s policymakers will don Scrooge masks when they meet on 17 December to deliver a message of austerity and sacrifice.

So sclerotic is the economy, so lacking in flexibility or productive spare capacity, that even the burst of growth experienced by the UK over the last year, defying most forecasters, must be calmed down with higher interest rates or else inflation will rip.

Huw Pill, the Bank’s chief economist, told the Financial Times on Saturday that more than one rate rise was almost certain.

Berdasarkan laporan, this is not a message anyone who borrows money will want to hear, especially when the festive season is in full swing. If interest rates edge up from 4% to 4. 25%, mortgage deals will rise and business loans will become more expensive.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the central bank expects businesses to react to the higher costs of doing business by hitting their customers with price hikes. It is an argument that presumes consumers have money available to pay higher prices, despite plenty of evidence to the contrary. Only households in the top half of the income scale have spent more this year and that has depended on running down their savings.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, consumers are also battle-hardened after the greedflation period following the pandemic that morphed into its evil cousin, shrinkflation. They know about grifting retailers and consumer product suppliers that try to build a narrative about the inevitability of surging inflation to disguise their own price hikes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the bank says its business surveys have failed to detect efforts by the corporate sector to increase prices. It’s just that a majority of policymakers are convinced pressure is building and inflation will be more than double their 2% target in a few months.

But if consumers don’t have any spare cash, or have become more savvy about how they spend it, there is still a weak link – a special kind of consumer who could aid corporates in pushing up prices.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the weak link is the state, or government in all its forms. The NHS is a big purchaser, so is local government and the many agencies that are funded by government, from Homes England to National Highways. Government expenditure on goods and services accounts for 25% of overall consumption in the economy.

Everything from concrete and medical supplies to food and furniture will cost more, and sellers will be prepared to justify the rise with a wide range of excuses.

Diungkapkan bahwa corporates will blame the war in the middle east for an increase in transport costs and the impact of climate change that makes growing stuff harder. They will even accuse the government of raising costs by introducing new worker protection rules.

Let’s add another one: contractors will say they can’t get the skilled staff and so must pass on the cost of higher wages.

After 15 years of austerity and job cuts, there is a question mark over whether the public sector has the nous and resolve to push back to keep costs in check.

Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning.

Berdasarkan laporan, budgets on the london to birmingham high-speed rail line (hs2) have spiralled out of control. The costs of the next largest infrastructure project in England, the 14. 5-mile (23km) lower Thames crossing linking Essex and Kent via two tunnels, have more than doubled to £11bn.

Sebagaimana diketahui, government spending on consultants reached £3. 7bn in 2024-25 from £2. 9bn in 2022-23 and there seems to be no end to their uses, from advisers on artificial intelligence to strategies for reaching net zero.

The public sector is also notorious for commissioning plans for new town or city developments for which there is no funding, except for the inflationary bill from consultants.

Diungkapkan bahwa these public sector organisations have huge clout, and should use it. If they do, there will be knock-on effects to inflation deals struck within the business community, which in many cases can only ramp up prices knowing the public sector is the ultimate buyer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, inside threadneedle street, policymakers expect everyone – consumers, government and business – to cave in to sellers’ demands. And that many of the UK’s 33 million workers will subsequently demand big pay rises to compensate.

Yet it must be possible that all three consumer groups will adopt the slogan Can’t Pay, Won’t Pay, limiting the rise in inflation and eliminating the need for elevated pay rises.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, even if the poor, financially bombed-out household consumer is the only one to take a stand against greedy corporates, inflation will not hit the heights forecast by the bank of england. In the meantime, it might have raised interest rates too far, laying waste to whatever growth there is in the economy.

Officials in South Sudan, the world’s youngest state, said on Saturday that its first national election would be postponed, raising new questions about a vote that analysts had already said could not yield a credible result.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the national elections commission said in a statement that the presidential and legislative elections, which had been scheduled for dec. 11 instead. 22, would be held on Feb. The country’s information minister, Ateny Wek Ateny, said the postponement would allow more time to register voters and educate them about the process.

Diungkapkan bahwa south sudan has never held a national election. Since gaining independence from Sudan in 2011 after decades of war, it has been ruled by President Salva Kiir, and it has faced seemingly intractable political difficulties.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2013, civil war broke out between the government and forces loyal to the main opposition leader, riek machar. Under a peace agreement to end the conflict in 2018, Mr. Machar became the vice president in a transitional government.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the upcoming election was supposed to underwrite that agreement. But the peace deal has unraveled since March 2025, when Mr. Machar was placed under house arrest in the capital, Juba, and charged with treason. In recent months, the government has replaced opposition lawmakers with its own supporters and dissolved the unity government.

Diungkapkan bahwa with mr. Machar effectively sidelined, there are no credible challengers to Mr. Kiir, who is widely expected to win the presidential election. He has a broad national following, and his party controls state institutions and the news media.

Diungkapkan bahwa the election faces stark logistical challenges. Civil servants have not been paid in more than a year, and parts of the country are controlled by armed groups, including Mr. Thousands of people have died in fighting and attacks on civilians. Machar’s forces. In March, more than 200 people were killed in a massacre in Unity State near the border with Sudan, according to human rights groups.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the conditions for credible polls are not currently in place,” the international crisis group said in a briefing for the u. Security Council this week. N. “Rushed elections could be a decisive final blow to the 2018 framework and would open the door to a return to sustained large-scale violence. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mr. Ateny, the information minister, acknowledged that the government could not gain access to “small parts” of the country, but said the election would be credible.

“It’s not always 100 percent, but it can be good for the sovereignty of the country and it’s good for the mandate of the state,” he said in an interview.

Berdasarkan laporan, in addition to the violence and civil unrest, south sudanese have been faced with soaring food prices, drought and flooding. Of the country’s roughly 12 million people, more than 8 million are in need of food assistance, according to the Famine Early Warning Systems Network, a globally recognized monitor of hunger.

Matthew Mpoke Bigg is the East Africa bureau chief for The New York Times, based in Nairobi, Kenya.

SpaceX's Starship spacecraft returned from its longest-yet flight in orbit on Saturday to the tower it was launched from on Friday.

Berdasarkan laporan, the spaceship descended and smoothly slipped between the mechanical "chopstick arms" above launch pad 2 in the us state of texas. It was the first key recovery of the rocket system's centerpiece vessel in the company's decadelong effort to develop a fully reusable rocket.

Diungkapkan bahwa "can you believe it?" spacex commentator dan huot shouted. "Look at her! Baby, she’s back!".

Berdasarkan laporan, it was the 15th test flight of the world's biggest and most powerful rocket system. SpaceX had intended to also capture the Super Heavy booster that launched the Starship, but the lower stage recovery was aborted and it exploded over the Gulf of Mexico shortly after launch on Friday.

The successful return of the craft's upper stage after orbiting Earth 14 times for over 22 hours, during which it deployed 26 Starlink satellites, marked a ​key milestone in the multibillion-dollar development of Starship, which billionaire Elon Musk sees ​as key to SpaceX's satellite business and ambitions to put humans on the moon and eventually Mars.

Berdasarkan laporan, nasa welcomed the news. The US space agency is paying billions of dollars for Starship to land Artemis astronauts on the moon later this decade and help build a permanent lunar base.

"It was almost magic," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman wrote on X.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as for the booster, spacex’s kate tice said its engines stopped firing too soon. The booster's guidance system sensed it was not in the correct position and initiated the self-destruction protocol. Engineers are still investigating the cause.

PM accuses Tories of burning ‘all our bridges’ and says deal he is pursuing with EU will ‘get food prices down’.

Andy Burnham has said the UK has “lost more than we gained” since leaving the EU, the prime minister’s latest in a string of comments criticising Brexit.

Outlining his desire to form closer ties with Brussels, Burnham accused the Conservative party of having “burned all our bridges” with the bloc after Brexit and said a new deal he hopes to secure with the EU next week will “get food prices down” and put more money in the pockets of British exporters.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the prime minister is due to meet european leaders at a summit next week and secure agreements that he says could raise gdp by 0. 4% – about £17bn – including on food and farming, emissions trading and a youth mobility scheme. He will also “explore options” for a different long-term relationship with Brussels.

Speaking at the Welsh Labour conference on Saturday, Burnham said: “We need to be willing to take difficult decisions to get the cost of living down.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it’s why, in a few days’ time, i will head to the next uk-eu summit and i will be working hard as we move towards it to get to a new deal on food and farming between the uk and the eu. Why am I doing that? Because I want to help Welsh businesses.

Diungkapkan bahwa the prime minister added: “i think we’ve lost more than we’ve gained over the last 10 years, and, actually, i think the conservatives gave britain a harsher and harder brexit than people thought they were getting when they voted in 2016, because they burned all of our bridges in the aftermath, with the eu, and so i’m going to lead as prime minister on this issue, and i’m going to go and try and get the best deal i can for wales, for those here who could benefit, welsh farmers, exporters of welsh shellfish and welsh lamb. ”.

Burnham has recently said he is open to rejoining the single market, customs union or to “go all the way” by rejoining the EU, but on Saturday he said voters would ultimately be “the boss” of any changes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he reiterated his commitment to labour’s manifesto “red lines” – which rule out returning to the customs union, single market or free movement. “People working together in unions, trade unions, but also unions of nations, and that’s what makes us who we are,” he told the conference.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “and, yes, working with the european union, as i said, but at the same time respecting the red lines in our manifesto and respecting the referendum, the referendum result. So, that’s the spirit, everybody, that I will take forward. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the government has already made several announcements that would tie the uk closer to brussels. Earlier this month, the Guardian reported that the UK was prepared to spend up to £450m a year to give EU students discounted university tuition fees, if Brussels allowed Britain access to the Made in Europe industrial programme.

Earlier this week, Hamish Falconer, the cabinet minister in charge of EU talks, said Britain was willing to discuss paying towards infrastructure schemes in poorer parts of the EU in return for access to the European electricity market.

Despite Burnham’s recent pro-EU comments, senior figures in Brussels have said they want to see the UK begin to start paying for access to the European schemes it says it wants access to.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the eu’s former brexit negotiator michel barnier told the bbc last week: “there will be no possibility to have one freedom and not the other. The four freedoms are clearly the four conditions to be inside a single market. ”.

Ursula von der Leyen, the president of the European Commission, and António Costa, who leads the European Council, will meet Burnham on 20 November in Brussels for a summit where deals on food and drink, carbon emissions and youth exchange could be signed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, barnier said the uk could not rejoin the single market “à la carte”, when speaking to the bbc’s laura kuenssberg last sunday, adding: “i said very, very often during these negotiations, the brexit, there is no cherrypicking. ”.

Peoria officials said a bomb was found at BioUrja Renewables and later defused; FBI said it is investigating.

Residents were ordered to evacuate parts of an Illinois community on Friday after the mayor there said authorities found a bomb at a local ethanol- and alcohol-production plant.

Diungkapkan bahwa the discovery reported at biourja renewables in peoria triggered a mandatory evacuation over a one-mile evacuation zone encompassing sections of that city as well as the adjacent municipality of east peoria. Officials ultimately lifted the evacuation zone at about 1. 25pm local time on Saturday – but only after making it clear there had genuinely been a bomb found and ruling out the presence of any other explosives.

Diungkapkan bahwa “it is real – this is a real thing,” peoria’s mayor, rita ali, initially said, according to local news outlet wmbd. We know it is a bomb. “We know that is a real threat. ”.

Peoria’s police chief, Brad Dixon, said at a news conference early on Saturday that explosives technicians had rendered the bomb in question safe.

But Dixon asked for the public’s patience as investigators searched BioUrja Renewals’ expansive facility for other explosive devices, as the Peoria news outlet WEEK reported.

“We don’t know if there are other devices,” Ali remarked.

Meanwhile, Ryan Presley of the FBI, who is in charge of the bureau’s field office about an hour away in Springfield, Illinois, said agents would pursue whoever was responsible “tirelessly” and “bring them to justice”.

No arrests had immediately been announced, with authorities saying updates would be provided as an investigation into the case continued.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at about 7. 05pm local time on Friday, the Peoria police department had announced that officers were “actively investigating a reported bomb threat at BioUrja Renewables”. The agency then urged “anyone who lives or works within a one-mile radius of the facility to immediately evacuate their homes and businesses until further notice”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the police’s statement said the evacuation notice had been “issued out of an abundance of caution while officers and emergency personnel investigate the threat”, which officials initially referred to as a suspicious package. The city offered the Manual Academy school as a temporary shelter, and police said anyone who needed assistance evacuating their home or business could call for help.

“Most streets in this area have been closed off,” police also said.

Diungkapkan bahwa in separate statement, the municipal government of neighboring east peoria acknowledged that the evacuation zone associated with the package at biourja renewables extended into part of that city. That area remained in effect as of 9am local time on Saturday, East Peoria’s government said.

A hockey game and a dance-themed charity event scheduled for Saturday had all been delayed, as WEEK reported.

And at least the Saturday portion of a Comic Con event scheduled to last through Sunday had been canceled, organizers said.

Diungkapkan bahwa “this is not a hoax,” the illinois state senator dave koehler said during the early saturday news conference. This is serious. “This has gone beyond that … This is serious. ”.

In the Saturday afternoon update, Peoria police said “state, federal, and local law enforcement had conducted an extensive search of the BioUrja facility [and] … found no other items of concern at this time”.

Police said the evacuation order implemented on Friday would no longer have effect, and any closed streets would be reopened.

“Residents are now free to return to their homes in the area that was affected by this order,” police added.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, law enforcement receive bomb threats and suspicious package calls not infrequently. Even though officials take those kinds of calls seriously as they investigate the claims, they often aren’t verified as credible or substantial.

Friday’s BioUrja Renewables case came amid a particularly chaotic day in the US marked by a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration-ordered nationwide ground stop at US airports that was in effect for about four hours, canceling or delaying more than 11,000 US flights.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the country’s nerves were also frayed by a tanker which struck a cruise ship docked on the mississippi river in new orleans on friday afternoon. But none of those injuries were critical, and there were no fatalities reported in association with the crash.

#594. Germany's 2027 budget: A record €561 billion and a mountain of debt

📅 14 Nov 2026

Germany's 2027 budget: A record €561 billion and a mountain of debt

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.dw.com/en/germany-s-2027-budget-a-record-€561-billion-and-a-mountain-of-debt/a-79943216?maca=en-rss-en-all-1573-rdf

Sebagaimana diketahui, the 2027 federal budget proposal has finally been hammered out and is set for a vote in parliament. What are the government's policy priorities in defense, infrastructure, the economy and social spending?.

Diungkapkan bahwa it was 5:55 a. m. on Friday when the Bundestag's Budget Committee concluded its final session.

Berdasarkan laporan, following nearly 16 hours of negotiations, lawmakers from the conservative christian democratic union(cdu) and christian social union (csu) parties, along with their coalition partners from the center-left social democratic party (spd), voted in favor of the 2027 draft budget. The opposition parties — the environmentalist Greens, the socialist Left Party and the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) — voted against it. With that, the way is now clear for the final vote in the Bundestag on November 27.

Sebagaimana diketahui, reading through the nearly 1,000-page document requires a great deal of number-crunching. Next year, the federal government plans to spend around €561 billion ($620 billion).

Sebagaimana diketahui, but here's the problem: it won't collect nearly enough revenue to cover these expenses. With a shortfall of €123 billion, borrowing will be needed to bridge the gap.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but that's not the only problem. On top of all this debt, Germany also has loans for defense spending and for the renovation of the dilapidated infrastructure. Approved by the Bundestag in 2025, these special funds are set to be in place for multiple years.

Berdasarkan laporan, if the new debt for 2027 is factored in, the total borrowing amounts to over €210 billion. This is the second-highest level of borrowing in the history of the Federal Republic of Germany. The only time Germany borrowed more was during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021, when borrowing reached €215. 4 billion.

Diungkapkan bahwa this development has drawn sharp criticism from opposition parties. Green Party lawmaker Sebastian Schäfer and his colleague Dietmar Bartsch of the Left Party called it a "gigantic mountain of debt," an "untrustworthy" budget, "irresponsible" policies at the expense of future generations and a lack of future prospects.

Berdasarkan laporan, to understand the reasons behind the growing debt, one has to look beyond the numbers. Every federal budget is a snapshot of the priorities set by a government and a country — in terms of the economy, social issues, security and geopolitics.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Berdasarkan laporan, for 2027, that story continues to be one of crises and wars. While Russia's war against Ukraine is driving up defense spending, the faltering economy is also demanding new investments. At the same time, Germany's population is aging rapidly, which is driving up social spending.

Berdasarkan laporan, what's more, the crumbling infrastructure must be repaired and modernized, and the energy transition is costing billions. And more than half of all this debt is going toward security and defense.

Diungkapkan bahwa russia's war against ukraine will enter its sixth year in 2027. As of the end of June, the federal government estimated its overall support for Ukraine to have reached approximately €100 billion. In response to a request from the AfD in the Bundestag, the government stated: "The federal government will continue to provide Ukraine with political, financial, humanitarian, civil and military support for as long as necessary. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the rearmament of the bundeswehr and spending on nato are also putting massive pressure on the budget. The defense budget is set to grow to just under €110 billion in 2027, an increase of around €27 billion compared to last year. Added to this are expenditures from the Bundeswehr's special fund.

Berdasarkan laporan, nevertheless, by far the largest single budget item comes from the ministry of labor and social affairs, which is set to grow to over €200 billion. There are plans for cost-cutting measures, for example, in basic income support for job seekers. But the costs of old-age pension benefits continue to rise.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, people born in the 1960s have begun to retire. Back then, more than 1 million children were born each year. But birth rates nearly halved in the early 1970s and have continued to decline since then. As a result, there will be an increasing number of retirees and a decreasing number of working-age individuals in the coming years.

Diungkapkan bahwa the pension funds cannot be financed by the pension contributions of this dwindling workforce and have to be subsidized by the government. Already, contributions to the pension insurance system — which are split equally between employees and employers — will have to be increased. They are expected to rise to just under 20% of gross salary.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the federal employment agency, too, has long been unable to make ends meet on contributions alone. In 2027, subsidies of more than €8 billion from the federal budget are planned.

Sebagaimana diketahui, anyone comparing germany's current budget situation with that of past years will be rubbing their eyes in disbelief. It wasn't that long ago that Germany was considered a model of fiscal discipline. Between 2014 and 2019, the federal budget managed to avoid taking on new debt for six consecutive years. In some years, there was even money left over.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Berdasarkan laporan, but the era of "balanced budgets" came to an abrupt end with the covid-19 pandemic in 2020. However, today Germany is still enjoying the benefits of those years of fiscal stability. Compared to other countries, Germany is still in relatively good shape.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the key indicator is not the amount of debt along but the debt-to-gdp ratio. It indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output.

Berdasarkan laporan, at the end of 2025, it stood at 63. However, in its latest fall report, the German Council of Economic Experts warned that Germany could be heading down a dangerous path. France, on the other hand, stands at over 110% and Italy at about 135% to 140%, while the US is well above 100%. 5% for Germany. If debt continues to rise at this rate, the debt-to-GDP ratio could climb to 100% by 2040.

Diungkapkan bahwa this would also put germany's creditworthiness on the financial markets at risk. This is the highest possible credit rating on the financial markets. Germany is the only country among the seven leading democratic industrialized nations (G7) that still holds a triple-A (AAA) rating. It signals to investors that the risk of default on German government bonds is extremely low.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this also means that interest rates on new loans are not set as high. This is an important point, as interest payments place an increasing burden on the federal budget each year. By 2027, approximately €42 billion in interest payments are expected to be due.

Diungkapkan bahwa at the end of november, the bundestag will hold its final debate on the draft budget. Should changes be expected by then? There is disagreement within the government over whether a reduction in the electricity tax might still be possible.

Berdasarkan laporan, the prospect of such a reduction had been raised by chancellor friedrich merz. On Friday, during a European leaders summit in Dublin, he reiterated: "I expect that we will discuss this again next Tuesday in the coalition committee, and I remain committed to my goal of lowering the electricity tax to the European minimum — in full — starting next year. ".

#595. Nigeria cautions against travel via Ethiopia's main airport due to altitude

📅 14 Nov 2026

Nigeria cautions against travel via Ethiopia's main airport due to altitude

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmz6qjpdy2wqo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Bole International Airport is a major travel hub.

Nigeria's government has cautioned its citizens, in particular those with medical conditions, against travelling via Ethiopia's main airport due to its altitude.

The foreign ministry in Abuja said 16 Nigerians with underlying health problems had died this year while transiting through Addis Ababa.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the city sits at an altitude of 2,334m (7,657ft) above sea level, making it one of the highest capitals in the world. Bole International Airport is a major hub for travel between Africa, the Middle East and Asia, serving millions of passengers a year.

Nigeria said those with cardiovascular and respiratory conditions were at an increased risk.

The Nigerian foreign ministry did not disclose the identities of the travellers it said had died, nor the cause of death.

It urged anyone with a health condition exacerbated by high altitudes to "exercise caution" when planning a journey via Addis Ababa and "obtain appropriate medical guidance" before doing so.

The ministry stressed that it did not want to discourage Nigerians from travelling through the Ethiopian capital.

Visiting an area at a high altitude can be dangerous for people with heart and lung diseases, as the air is thinner and so less oxygen can get into the bloodstream, experts say.

This means the heart has to work harder to get enough oxygen to different parts of the body, which can sometimes lead to heart failure among those with existing conditions, according to the American Heart Association.

The lack of oxygen at high altitudes can cause adverse effects such as dizziness, fatigue and shortness of breath among healthy people - which can cause complications for people with lung disease, studies show.

The Trump administration says Friday’s four-hour nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop that delayed or canceled thousands of flight stemmed from routine maintenance.

At a news briefing on Saturday, the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, said that the issues began when a contractor was performing “routine maintenance” at a remote FAA facility to “switch telecommunications lines” from copper wire to fiber optic cable.

Diungkapkan bahwa “what we’re working to determine is whether we had incompetence,” duffy said, “or did they install a faulty router. ”.

He added: “Once we were able to isolate the work that was being done at this remote location, all of our systems came back online,” and the ground stop was lifted.

However, travel chaos continued across the US on Saturday.

At the briefing, the FAA’s head, Bryan Bedford, apologized to passengers and said he believed that the worst of the disruption “is behind us”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we will still have delays and cancellations today, but that will set us up for a full recovery tomorrow,” bedford said. “Based on everything that we’re hearing from our airline partners, they believe that they’ll be able to have full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i want to reiterate: we see zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything ai-related,” he continued. “So we want to be clear that we have a equipment issue, and we’re working through what this defective piece of equipment was. ”.

Later on Saturday, L3Harris, the federal contractor that Duffy said had been updating air traffic control equipment before the ground stop, released a statement saying that it took the ground stop and its negative effects “on travelers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously”.

“We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the [Friday] ground stop of our nation’s air travel,” the contractor said.

On Saturday,airlines worked to recover from Friday’s four-hour nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop that delayed or canceled thousands of flights.

The disruption, which marked the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years, left passengers stranded at airports across the country and facing uncertainty about when they could reach their destinations.

Duffy on Friday had blamed the ground stop on an ageing air control system, saying that the communications equipment became “overloaded with data” and was starting to cause inconsistency in the data”.

“Because of that, we shut the system down,” Duffy said.

Berdasarkan laporan, duffy on saturday again mentioned the us having a “decades-old air traffic control system”. “It’s not just old equipment – we have an incredibly old telecommunications system,” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the work happening was due to the age of the copper wire that we were replacing,” duffy said on saturday. “What we’re working determine was whether … it [was] user error or installer error. ”.

Duffy echoed Bedford in saying “we don’t believe” the disruption resulted from a cyber-attack or some hostile foreign nation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “this was an faa system that didn’t meet the moment,” he said. “Our contractor didn’t meet the moment or the equipment didn’t meet the moment and causes the outages. ”.

Duffy also warned that it would “take us time” to “resume normal operations”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, among those affected by the fallout from the ground stop on friday were sports teams traveling for games over the weekend. In college football, the Southeastern Conference announced that Mississippi’s game against Oklahoma had been rescheduled to Sunday – a day usually reserved for the National Football League (NFL).

Berdasarkan laporan, meanwhile, a men’s college basketball game between the university of north carolina greensboro and cornell university, scheduled for saturday, was postponed. NBA and NHL travel was also disrupted for the weekend.

On Saturday morning, there were reported flight disruptions at airports in major cities including Boston, Washington DC, New York and Miami.

American Airlines said in a statement on Saturday that “while we are taking every step to limit the impact on our customers and team members, the lingering effects of this major disruption to the national airspace system will continue today, including additional delays and cancellations”.

Delta Air Lines also warned passengers traveling on Saturday that they “should expect delays and additional schedule adjustments as we work to reposition flight crews and aircraft” after the FAA-ordered ground stop.

The UK’s Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) also issued a statement on Saturday morning warning that “while US flights have resumed, there may be some follow-on disruption as airlines work to re-book affected passengers and get all services back to normal”.

Diungkapkan bahwa friday marked the third nationwide ground stop issued by the faa this century. The first occurred after the 11 September 2001 terrorist attacks. And the second took place in January 2023, during the Biden administration, after a pilot notification system went down.

Diungkapkan bahwa meanwhile, on saturday, new york’s governor, kathy hochul, a democrat, called on duffy to resign. She also called on Congress to “launch a full investigation to determine what went wrong and ensure it never happens again”.

#598. Nigeria's upcoming election marred by rising AI disinformation
